cards.t: Health risks of prolonged ICT use
cards.tz: 长时间使用 ICT 的健康风险
cards.en:
Intuition: your body is built to move. If you sit still and repeat the same small movement for hours (typing, scrolling), some body parts get overused and others get no blood flow.

The five risks in the book:

RiskWhat it isCause
Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI)pain or numbness in fingers/wriststhe same movement again and again (clicking, typing)
Eyestraintired eyes, blurred visionstaring at a screen too long, bad lighting, glare
Back and neck problemsaches, "tech neck"poor posture, sitting still too long
Deep vein thrombosis (DVT)a blood clot in a leg veinsitting for very long periods; can be fatal if the clot moves to the lungs
Tired legsleg fatiguefeet not supported / hanging

Exam wording: health risk + cause + solution, e.g. "RSI in the wrist, caused by repetitive mouse clicking; use a mouse pad with wrist rest to keep the wrist straight."
cards.zh:
直觉：身体需要活动。长时间坐着不动、重复同一个小动作（打字、滑屏），某些部位被过度使用，另一些部位血液不流通。

课本五种风险：

风险是什么成因
RSI 重复性劳损手指/手腕痛、麻重复动作（点鼠标、打字）
Eyestrain 眼疲劳眼累、视线模糊盯屏幕太久、光线差、反光
Back and neck problems腰背颈痛、tech neck姿势差、久坐不动
Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) 深静脉血栓腿部静脉血块久坐；血块流到肺部可致命
Tired legs 腿部疲劳腿累脚没有承托

考试写法：健康风险 + 成因 + 解决方法，例如 "RSI in the wrist, caused by repetitive mouse clicking; use a mouse pad with wrist rest."

ex.q: Ada programs for 8 hours every day. Name one health risk and an ergonomic product to reduce it.
ex.a:
1. Find the repeated action: typing and clicking all day.
2. Risk: RSI in wrist/fingers.
3. Product: mouse pad with wrist rest or ergonomic keyboard, keeps the wrist straight.
ex.az: 1. 找重复动作：整天打字点鼠标。2. 风险：RSI。3. 产品：带护腕鼠标垫/人体工学键盘，手腕保持平直。

ex.q: Ben watches videos on a long-haul flight for 12 hours without standing up. Which risk is most serious, and why?
ex.a:
1. Long sitting without moving → blood flows slowly in legs.
2. Risk: deep vein thrombosis (blood clot).
3. Serious because the clot can travel to the lungs and be fatal.
4. Fix: stand up and walk/stretch every hour.
ex.az: 1. 久坐不动→腿部血流慢。2. 深静脉血栓。3. 血块流到肺部可致命。4. 每小时起身活动。

ex.q: Carol's eyes feel dry and her vision is blurred after gaming in a dark room. Identify the risk and two causes.
ex.a:
1. Risk: eyestrain.
2. Cause 1: staring at the monitor too long without rest.
3. Cause 2: bad lighting (bright screen, dark room).
4. Fix: 20-20-20 rule, turn on room lights.
ex.az: 1. 眼疲劳。2. 盯屏幕太久。3. 光线差。4. 20-20-20 法则、开灯。

ex.q: A student writes: "Eyestrain is caused by repetitive typing; use a footrest." What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Eyestrain comes from looking at the screen too long / bad lighting, not typing.
2. A footrest helps tired legs / posture, not eyes.
3. Correct: "Eyestrain, caused by staring at the monitor for too long; take breaks with the 20-20-20 rule and use window blinds to reduce glare."
Lesson: the cause and the solution must match the risk.
ex.az: 1. 眼疲劳成因是盯屏幕、光线，不是打字。2. 脚踏是解决腿部问题。3. 风险、成因、方法要对应。

cards.t: Correct sitting posture and workstation set-up
cards.tz: 正确坐姿与工作台设置
cards.en:
Intuition: set up the desk so your body stays in a relaxed, natural position: like standing straight, but sitting.

Fig. 2.3 checklist (top to bottom):

  • Ergonomic monitor: adjustable height and angle; eyes look slightly downward (about 30°), so the neck is not bent.
  • Window blinds: block strong sunlight and reduce glare (reflections) on the screen.
  • Armrest: adjustable; forearms horizontal and relaxed.
  • Mouse pad with wrist rest: wrist straight → less RSI.
  • Ergonomic chair: adjustable height and back rest; knees about 90°.
  • Footrest: feet flat → less leg fatigue.

No footrest? Lower the chair, then adjust the table and monitor height/angle to match.

Exam wording: "adjust the monitor so that the viewing angle is slightly downward", "keep the forearm horizontal", "keep the wrist straight", "keep the feet flat on the floor / footrest".
cards.zh:
直觉：把桌椅调到身体自然放松的姿势，好像"坐着的站直"。

Fig. 2.3 检查清单（由上到下）：

  • Ergonomic monitor：高度、角度可调；视线稍向下（约30°），不弯颈。
  • Window blinds 百叶帘：挡强光，减少屏幕反光 (glare)。
  • Armrest 扶手：可调；前臂水平放松。
  • Mouse pad with wrist rest：手腕平直，减少 RSI。
  • Ergonomic chair：高度、椅背可调；膝盖约 90°。
  • Footrest 脚踏：双脚平放，减少腿累。

没有脚踏？调低椅子，再相应调整桌子和显示器高度/角度。

考试写法：viewing angle slightly downward / forearm horizontal / wrist straight / feet flat。

ex.q: Peter's feet hang above the floor. (a) Which product helps? (b) Without it, what should he adjust?
ex.a:
(a) A footrest.
(b) 1. Lower the chair until feet are flat.
2. Then lower the table and adjust the monitor height and angle so posture is still correct. (Textbook Checkpoint 2.1 Q5: all of these.)
ex.az: (a) 脚踏。(b) 调低椅子，再调桌子和显示器高度角度。

ex.q: Sunlight from a window makes reflections on Kelly's screen. Suggest one item and explain.
ex.a:
1. Problem: glare → eyestrain.
2. Item: window blinds.
3. They block strong sunlight and reduce light reflection on the screen.
ex.az: 1. 反光→眼疲劳。2. 百叶帘。3. 挡强光，减少屏幕反光。

ex.q: Tom places his monitor high so he looks upward at it. Is this correct?
ex.a:
1. Correct viewing angle is slightly downward (about 30°).
2. Looking up bends the neck backward → neck pain.
3. Fix: lower the monitor so the top is at or below eye level.
ex.az: 1. 应稍向下看。2. 仰头会颈痛。3. 调低显示器。

ex.q: A student says: "An ergonomic chair alone is enough for a correct workstation." What is the mistake?
ex.a:
1. A chair only supports back and legs.
2. Wrist (RSI), eyes (glare), neck (monitor angle) still need the wrist rest, blinds, adjustable monitor.
3. Correct: a workstation is a set of adjustments that must fit together.
ex.az: 椅子只照顾背和腿；手腕、眼睛、颈部还需要护腕、百叶帘、可调显示器，要整体配合。

frames.zh: 扶手令前臂水平；护腕令手腕平直。

frames.en: Back rest supports the lower back; knees about 90°.
frames.zh: 椅背承托腰部，膝盖约90°。

frames.en: Feet flat on the floor or a footrest.
frames.zh: 双脚平放地上或脚踏。

cards.tz: 手机与平板的正确姿势
cards.en:
Intuition: your head weighs about 5 kg. The more you bend it down to a phone, the harder your neck muscles have to pull.

Problems:

  • Tech neck: neck/shoulder pain from looking down at a phone.
  • Text claw: finger/wrist pain from typing on a small touch screen (a kind of RSI).

Correct practice (Fig. 2.4):

  • Phone: keep the phone at eye level.
  • Tablet: lift it up with a pillow or stand.
  • Long typing: tablet stand + external keyboard. Stand → screen at eye level (neck). Keyboard → wrists natural (RSI).
  • Rest reminder app: it pushes a rest notification. It does not force-close apps or switch the device off.

Exam wording: "Raise the screen to eye level so the user need not bend the neck."
cards.zh:
直觉：头约重 5 kg，越低头看手机，颈部肌肉越吃力。

问题：

  • Tech neck：低头看手机造成颈肩痛。
  • Text claw：在小屏幕打字造成手指手腕痛（属 RSI）。

正确做法：

  • 手机：举到视线高度。
  • 平板：用枕头或支架垫高。
  • 长时间打字：支架 + 外接键盘。支架护颈，键盘护手腕。
  • 休息提醒 app：推送休息通知，不会强制关 app 或关机。

考试写法：Raise the screen to eye level so the user need not bend the neck.

ex.q: George types essays on a tablet with a stand and a wireless keyboard. How is each item ergonomic?
ex.a:
1. Stand: raises the screen to a suitable height/viewing angle → no bending neck → less neck and back pain.
2. Keyboard: placed so forearms are horizontal and wrists straight; physical keys are easier than touch screen → less RSI.
ex.az: 1. 支架：屏幕升高，减少颈背痛。2. 键盘：手腕平直，减少 RSI。

ex.q: Mia reads on her phone in bed with the phone on her chest, chin down. Give the risk and a fix.
ex.a:
1. Chin down → neck bent → tech neck (neck/shoulder pain).
2. Fix: hold the phone at eye level, or prop it on a pillow/stand.
ex.az: 1. 低头→tech neck。2. 把手机举到视线高度或用枕头支架。

ex.q: Which describes a good rest reminder app? A. shuts down the phone after 1 hour B. pushes a rest notification C. deletes games
ex.a:
1. Its job is to remind, not to control.
2. Answer: B, it pushes a rest notification.
ex.az: 提醒 app 只负责提醒：答案 B。

ex.q: A student answers: "Using a tablet stand reduces RSI." Why is this not the best answer?
ex.a:
1. A stand changes the screen height, so it mainly protects the neck/back.
2. RSI is a wrist/finger problem; the external keyboard reduces RSI.
3. Match each item with the body part it protects.
ex.az: 支架主要护颈背；RSI 要靠外接键盘。产品要配对正确部位。

cards.tz: 人体工学的定义与目的
cards.en:
Intuition: a shoe shop sells many sizes because feet differ. Ergonomics does the same for tools: the design fits the person, not the person forcing himself to fit the design.

Definition (learn it): Ergonomics is a science-based discipline about designing or arranging workplaces, products and systems to suit the people who use them.

Aim: optimise the strengths and abilities of people and minimise the risk of injury or harm, by improving tools and environments for working, resting and playing.

Why so many things are adjustable: users have different body sizes, so chair height, armrests and monitor angle can change.

Example: gaming chair sales rose over 50% in 2020 because of comfortable material and ergonomic design (adjustable seat, back rest, armrests). In-ear headphones, mice and keyboards are ergonomic products too.

Exam wording: "to suit the people who use them" and "minimise the risk of injury".
cards.zh:
直觉：鞋店卖不同尺码，因为脚不同。人体工学对工具也一样：设计迁就人，不是人迁就设计。

定义（要背）：Ergonomics is a science-based discipline about designing or arranging workplaces, products and systems to suit the people who use them.

目的：optimise the strengths and abilities of people and minimise the risk of injury or harm。

为何很多东西可调：每个人身材不同，所以椅高、扶手、显示器角度可调。

例子：2020 年电竞椅销量升超过 50%，因为物料舒适和人体工学设计（座椅、椅背、扶手可调）。耳机、鼠标、键盘也是人体工学产品。

考试写法：to suit the people who use them / minimise the risk of injury。

ex.q: Why do ergonomic chairs have adjustable height?
ex.a:
1. Users have different heights and leg lengths.
2. Adjustable height lets each user keep feet flat and knees about 90°.
3. So the product suits the person who uses it.
ex.az: 1. 人人高度不同。2. 可调让每人双脚平放、膝盖约90°。3. 设计迁就用户。

ex.q: Explain why gaming chairs became popular in 2020.
ex.a:
1. People stayed home and sat for hours (gaming, online classes).
2. Gaming chairs have comfortable material and ergonomic design: adjustable seat, back rest, armrests.
3. They support the body during long sitting and reduce back/neck pain.
ex.az: 1. 在家久坐。2. 物料舒适、可调设计。3. 承托身体，减少腰颈痛。

ex.q: Is a vertical mouse an example of ergonomics? Explain with the definition.
ex.a:
1. Definition: design products to suit the people who use them.
2. A vertical mouse holds the hand in a natural handshake position.
3. This avoids twisting the wrist and minimises the risk of RSI. So yes.
ex.az: 符合定义：手呈握手姿势，避免扭腕，减少 RSI。

ex.q: A student defines ergonomics as "making computers faster so users save time." What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Speed of the computer is performance, not ergonomics.
2. Ergonomics is about fitting the design to people and reducing injury.
3. Write the textbook definition.
ex.az: 电脑快是性能，不是人体工学；人体工学是设计迁就人、减少受伤。

cards.tz: 电脑用的人体工学产品
cards.en:
Intuition: each product fixes one body part. Learn them as problem → product pairs.

ProductHow it helps
Ergonomic (vertical) mousehand in a natural handshake position, avoids twisting the wrist → less RSI
Mouse pad with wrist restkeeps the wrist straight → less RSI
Ergonomic (split/curved) keyboardnatural hand and wrist angle → less RSI
Adjustable laptop standraises the screen to eye level → less neck pain
Ergonomic chairadjustable height, back/arm/neck rest → less back/neck pain
Dual monitorsless switching between windows; place both at arm's length and use a swivel chair to avoid twisting the neck

Summary: RSI → wrist rest, ergonomic mouse/keyboard, armrest. Eyestrain → blinds, enough lighting. Tired legs → footrest. Back/neck → chair with back and neck rest, adjustable monitor.

Exam wording: name the product, then "keeps the wrist straight / raises the screen to eye level, reducing RSI / neck pain".
cards.zh:
直觉：每件产品照顾一个身体部位，用问题 → 产品来记。

产品作用
Ergonomic (vertical) mouse手呈握手姿势，避免扭腕→减少 RSI
Mouse pad with wrist rest手腕平直→减少 RSI
Ergonomic keyboard（分体/弧形）手和手腕角度自然→减少 RSI
Adjustable laptop stand屏幕升到视线高度→减少颈痛
Ergonomic chair可调高度、椅背、扶手、头枕→减少腰颈痛
Dual monitors少切换视窗；两屏放在一臂距离，用转椅避免扭颈

总结：RSI→护腕、人体工学鼠标键盘、扶手；眼疲劳→百叶帘、足够照明；腿累→脚踏；腰颈痛→有头枕椅背的椅、可调显示器。

ex.q: Mr Lee uses a laptop on a low desk and his neck hurts. Suggest a product.
ex.a:
1. Problem: screen too low → bending neck.
2. Product: adjustable laptop stand (with an external keyboard and mouse).
3. It raises the screen to eye level, reducing neck pain.
ex.az: 1. 屏幕太低→低头。2. 可调手提电脑支架。3. 屏幕升到视线高度。

ex.q: A video editor uses dual monitors. How should she arrange them?
ex.a:
1. Put both monitors at about arm's length.
2. Use a swivel chair to turn the whole body instead of twisting the neck.
3. Benefit: less switching between windows, and no neck strain.
ex.az: 1. 两屏放一臂距离。2. 用转椅转身，不扭颈。

ex.q: Match: (i) RSI (ii) eyestrain (iii) tired legs with: footrest / window blinds / vertical mouse.
ex.a:
1. RSI → vertical mouse (no wrist twist).
2. Eyestrain → window blinds (less glare).
3. Tired legs → footrest.
ex.az: RSI→直立鼠标；眼疲劳→百叶帘；腿累→脚踏。

ex.q: "A footrest reduces RSI in the wrist." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. A footrest supports the feet/legs; it helps tired legs and posture.
2. Wrist RSI needs a wrist rest, ergonomic mouse or keyboard.
3. Always match the product to the body part.
ex.az: 脚踏是护腿；手腕 RSI 要用护腕或人体工学鼠标键盘。

cards.t: Taking breaks: the 20-20-20 rule and stretching
cards.tz: 休息习惯：20-20-20 法则与伸展
cards.en:
Intuition: furniture helps, but no chair fixes sitting still for 5 hours. Muscles and eyes need a change.

Rules:

  • 20-20-20 rule (eyestrain): every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet (6 m) away for 20 seconds. The eye muscles relax and refocus.
  • Muscle strain: take a 5-minute break to stretch and move every hour. This also lowers the risk of DVT.
  • New habits are hard → use break reminder software (e.g. EyeRest).

Exam wording: "take regular breaks and exercise"; "every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds".
cards.zh:
直觉：家具有帮助，但没有椅子能解决连续坐 5 小时。肌肉和眼睛需要转换。

  • 20-20-20 法则（防眼疲劳）：每 20 分钟，望 20 英尺（6 米）外的东西 20 秒，令眼肌放松、重新对焦。
  • 肌肉劳损：每小时休息 5 分钟，伸展活动，也减低 DVT 风险。
  • 新习惯难养成→用休息提醒软件（如 EyeRest）。

考试写法：take regular breaks and exercise; every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds。

ex.q: Jason studies online from 7:00 pm to 9:00 pm. Using the 20-20-20 rule, how many eye breaks should he take?
ex.a:
1. 2 hours = 120 minutes.
2. 120 ÷ 20 = 6 → breaks at 7:20, 7:40, 8:00, 8:20, 8:40 (and 9:00 when he stops).
3. So 5 breaks during the session, each: look 6 m away for 20 s.

ex.q: Explain how the 20-20-20 rule reduces eyestrain.
ex.a:
1. Looking at a near screen keeps eye focusing muscles tight.
2. Looking far away lets them relax and refocus.
3. Doing it every 20 minutes stops tiredness building up.
ex.az: 近看令眼肌紧张；望远令眼肌放松、重新对焦。

ex.q: An office worker sits 4 hours without moving. Suggest a habit and name the risks it lowers.
ex.a:
1. Habit: 5-minute stretch/walk every hour, using a break reminder app.
2. Lowers: muscle strain, back/neck pain, and deep vein thrombosis.
ex.az: 每小时伸展 5 分钟；减少肌肉劳损、腰颈痛、DVT。

ex.q: A student writes the 20-20-20 rule as "every 20 seconds, look 20 metres away for 20 minutes". Fix it.
ex.a:
1. The units are mixed up.
2. Correct: every 20 minutes, look 20 feet (≈6 m) away for 20 seconds.
Tip: minutes → feet → seconds (big gap, far, short).
ex.az: 单位错了：每 20 分钟，望 20 英尺（6 米），20 秒。

frames.en: Start working at the screen.
frames.zh: 开始用屏幕。

frames.en: Look at something 6 m away for 20 s.
frames.zh: 望 6 米外 20 秒。

frames.en: Repeat the 20-20-20 break.
frames.zh: 再做一次。

frames.en: Stand up, stretch and walk for 5 minutes (muscles, DVT).
frames.zh: 起身伸展 5 分钟。

cards.en:
Intuition: ergonomics also applies to software. A badly designed app does not hurt your wrist, but it hurts your patience and causes mistakes.

Ergonomics considers not only body size and dominant hand, but also the user's age, strength, technological experience, skill/knowledge, cultural expectation and goals.

User-friendly interface features:

  • Zoom / adjustable font size for users with poor eyesight.
  • Consistent terms throughout the app.
  • Grouping options (e.g. stations grouped by rail line, not one long list).
  • Sufficient colour contrast between text and background.
  • Clear navigation and help texts.

A lack of ergonomic design frustrates users. Note: a log-in password is a security feature, not an ergonomic one.

Exam wording: "user-friendly", "reduces the user's effort / errors".
cards.zh:
直觉：人体工学也适用于软件。设计差的 app 不会伤手腕，但会令人烦躁、出错。

除身材、惯用手外，还要考虑用户的年龄、力气、科技经验、技能知识、文化预期和目标。

  • 放大 (zoom) / 可调字体大小：照顾视力差的人。
  • 用词一致。
  • 分组选项（车站按路线分组）。
  • 足够颜色对比。
  • 清晰导航和说明文字。

缺乏人体工学设计会令用户沮丧。注意：登入密码是保安功能，不是人体工学。

ex.q: An MTR ticket app lists 100 stations alphabetically. Suggest an improvement.
ex.a:
1. A long list is slow to search.
2. Group stations by rail line (or add search).
3. Users find their station faster with less effort.
ex.az: 按路线分组，用户更快找到车站。

ex.q: Grandma finds text in a banking app too small. Which two features help?
ex.a:
1. Adjustable font size / zoom.
2. Sufficient colour contrast between text and background.
ex.az: 可调字体、足够颜色对比。

ex.q: An app uses "Delete" on one page and "Remove" / "Erase" on others for the same action. What principle is broken?
ex.a:
1. Same action, different words → users get confused.
2. It breaks consistency (consistent terms).
3. Use one term everywhere.
ex.az: 同一动作用不同字，违反一致性。

ex.q: "Adding two-factor log-in makes the app more ergonomic." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Two-factor log-in protects data security.
2. It actually adds steps, so it is not an ergonomic/user-friendly feature.
3. Ergonomic examples: zoom, consistent terms, contrast.
ex.az: 双重认证是保安功能，反而多步骤，不是人体工学。

cards.tz: 界面设计准则：一致、效率、记忆
cards.en:
Intuition: a good app works like a well-signed MTR station: same signs everywhere, short paths, nothing to memorise.

GuidelineMeaning
Consistencysaves time adapting; keep terminologies, action sequences and graphics consistent
Efficiencyfeatures for both inexperienced and advanced users; break complex tasks into simpler tasks; less is more, avoid distraction; acceptable waiting time
Memoryminimise users' memory load: generic actions, universal signages (icons people know), clear navigations and help texts

Example: a date-of-birth input split into Year / Month / Day drop-downs with a specific error ("Select your birth month") beats one text box "2033/14/12" with only "Error".

Exam wording: use the guideline name + its phrase, e.g. "Memory: minimise users' memory load by using universal signages."
cards.zh:
直觉：好 app 像指示清楚的港铁站：标志一致、路径短、不用记东西。

准则意思
Consistency 一致用词、操作次序、图像一致，减少适应时间
Efficiency 效率照顾新手和熟手；复杂工作拆成简单步骤；少即是多；等待时间可接受
Memory 记忆减少用户记忆负担：通用动作、通用标志、清晰导航和说明

例子：出生日期分成年/月/日选单，错误信息具体（"Select your birth month"），好过一个文字框加"Error"。

ex.q: A sign-up form has one box for date of birth and shows only "Error". Improve it using the guidelines.
ex.a:
1. Efficiency: split into Year / Month / Day drop-downs (simpler tasks).
2. Memory: add placeholders (YYYY) so users need not remember the format.
3. Give a specific error such as "Select your birth month" (help text).
ex.az: 拆成年月日选单；加提示；错误信息要具体。

ex.q: A photo app has a "basic" mode and a "pro" mode with manual settings. Which guideline?
ex.a:
1. It serves both inexperienced and advanced users.
2. Guideline: Efficiency.
ex.az: 照顾新手和熟手：效率。

ex.q: Why use a 🗑 bin icon for delete instead of a new symbol?
ex.a:
1. Users already know the bin means delete.
2. This is a universal signage, it minimises memory load.
3. Guideline: Memory.
ex.az: 通用标志，减少记忆负担。

ex.q: A student says a homepage full of flashing banners and 30 buttons is "efficient because everything is there". What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Too many items distract users and slow them down.
2. Guideline says less is more, avoid distraction.
3. Show only key functions; hide advanced ones in menus.
ex.az: 太多元素令人分心；应少即是多。

cards.t: Misconception: ergonomics is only about furniture
cards.tz: 误解：人体工学只关于家具
cards.en:
Wrong idea: "Ergonomics only means comfortable chairs and desks."

Correct idea: ergonomics covers three areas:

  1. Physical products: chair, mouse, keyboard, stand, footrest, blinds.
  2. Work habits: breaks, 20-20-20 rule, stretching.
  3. Software / user interface design: consistency, efficiency, memory load, contrast, font size.

The Chapter Summary says: "Ergonomics is not only related to the furniture and workstation set-up. Ergonomic and user-friendly features are important in software design."

Two more traps:

  • Security features (password, anti-virus) protect data; they are not ergonomic.
  • The product must match the problem: a footrest does not stop wrist RSI.
cards.zh:
错误："人体工学只是舒服的桌椅。"

正确：包括三方面：

  1. 实体产品：椅、鼠标、键盘、支架、脚踏、百叶帘。
  2. 工作习惯：休息、20-20-20、伸展。
  3. 软件/界面设计：一致、效率、记忆负担、对比、字体。

课本总结："Ergonomics is not only related to the furniture and workstation set-up. Ergonomic and user-friendly features are important in software design."

另外两个陷阱：保安功能（密码、防毒）不是人体工学；产品要配对问题（脚踏不能防手腕 RSI）。

ex.q: Which are ergonomic designs? (1) adjustable font size (2) anti-virus software (3) footrest (4) break reminder app
ex.a:
1. (1) software UI → yes.
2. (2) security → no.
3. (3) product → yes.
4. (4) habit support → yes.
Answer: (1), (3), (4).

ex.q: Give one ergonomic example from each area: product, habit, software.
ex.a:
1. Product: mouse pad with wrist rest.
2. Habit: 20-20-20 rule.
3. Software: consistent icons and terms.
ex.az: 产品：护腕垫；习惯：20-20-20；软件：一致的图标用词。

ex.q: A school buys new chairs and says "our computer room is now fully ergonomic". What else is missing?
ex.a:
1. Monitors may still be at the wrong height/angle; glare from windows.
2. Students may not take breaks.
3. Add adjustable monitors, blinds, wrist rests, break reminders.
ex.az: 还要调显示器、百叶帘、护腕、休息提醒。

ex.q: "A strong password makes an app more user-friendly." Why is this a mistake?
ex.a:
1. A password improves security, not comfort or efficiency.
2. It adds effort for the user.
3. Keep security and ergonomics separate in answers.
ex.az: 密码是保安，不是人体工学，反而增加负担。

cards.tz: 网络成瘾的征兆和症状
cards.en:
Intuition: the line between a habit and an addiction is control. A habit: you surf 1-2 hours after finishing your work. An addiction: you cannot stop, and you end up late for or missing important tasks.

Signs and symptoms (book):

  • Prioritising Internet use over necessary life tasks
  • Thinking about the Internet even when offline (e.g. during lessons)
  • Being moody and irritable when Internet access is restricted

Types: online game addiction, social media addiction, compulsive video streaming, gadget addiction.

Watching one movie every night by plan is not a symptom: it is a controlled leisure habit.

Exam wording: quote the three signs word for word.
cards.zh:
直觉：习惯和成瘾的分别在于能否控制。完成功课后上网 1-2 小时是习惯；停不了、甚至迟到或错过重要事情就很可能是成瘾。

征兆：

  • Prioritising Internet use over necessary life tasks 把上网放在必要事务之前
  • Thinking about the Internet even when offline 离线时（如上课）也想着上网
  • Being moody and irritable when Internet access is restricted 被限制上网时烦躁易怒

类型：网络游戏、社交媒体、强迫性追剧、电子产品成瘾。

每晚按计划看一部电影不是症状。

ex.q: Kevin plays games until 3 am and often misses his first lesson. Habit or addiction? Why?
ex.a:
1. He cannot stop (plays until 3 am).
2. He misses important tasks (lessons).
3. Sign: prioritising Internet use over necessary life tasks → likely addiction.
ex.az: 停不了、错过上课→成瘾。

ex.q: Lily gets angry and slams the door when her parents turn off the Wi-Fi. Which sign?
ex.a: Being moody and irritable when Internet access is restricted.
ex.az: 被限制上网时烦躁易怒。

ex.q: During a maths test, Max keeps thinking about his game's daily reward. Which sign?
ex.a: Thinking about the Internet even when offline.
ex.az: 离线时也想着上网。

ex.q: "Nina watches one 2-hour movie every Saturday night after homework, so she is addicted." Agree?
ex.a:
1. It is planned and done after her tasks.
2. She is in control; no task is missed.
3. So it is a habit, not an addiction. Time alone does not decide it; loss of control does.
ex.az: 有计划、完成功课后才看→习惯，不是成瘾；关键是失控。

cards.en:
Intuition: hours spent online are taken from sleep, exercise and people. So addiction hurts the body, the mind and relationships.

Physical healthMental health
Fatigue
Muscle strain
Poor sleep
Unintentional weight loss/gain		Poor memory
Anxiety and depression
Concentration difficulty

These lead to poor social relationships and a decrease in quality of life (Fig. 2.10). Social side: arguments with family, isolation, phubbing.

Extreme case (Activity 2.2): a 17-year-old played online games for 40 hours non-stop, argued with his family and died by suicide.

Diseases like diabetes are not listed as a direct result.

Exam wording: give one physical and one mental impact, plus poor social relationships.
cards.zh:
直觉：上网的时间从睡眠、运动、与人相处中扣出来，所以成瘾会伤身、伤心、伤关系。

身体精神
疲劳、肌肉劳损、睡眠差、体重不正常增减记忆差、焦虑抑郁、难以集中

结果是人际关系差和生活质素下降；社交方面：和家人争吵、孤立、phubbing。

极端例子：17 岁少年连续玩游戏 40 小时，与家人争吵后自杀。

糖尿病等疾病不是课本列出的直接后果。

ex.q: State two physical and two mental impacts of Internet addiction.
ex.a:
1. Physical: fatigue, poor sleep (also muscle strain, weight change).
2. Mental: anxiety and depression, concentration difficulty (also poor memory).
ex.az: 身体：疲劳、睡眠差；精神：焦虑抑郁、难集中。

ex.q: Explain how gaming addiction can lower exam results.
ex.a:
1. Late-night gaming → poor sleep and fatigue.
2. Leads to concentration difficulty and poor memory in class.
3. Less revision time → lower results.
ex.az: 睡眠差→难集中、记忆差→成绩下降。

ex.q: How does Internet addiction affect social relationships?
ex.a:
1. Less face-to-face time with family/friends.
2. Arguments when access is limited; phubbing makes others feel ignored.
3. Result: isolation, poor social relationships.
ex.az: 少相处、争吵、phubbing→关系差。

ex.q: A student lists "diabetes" as a direct impact from the textbook. Comment.
ex.a:
1. The book lists fatigue, muscle strain, poor sleep, weight change.
2. Diabetes is not a listed direct result.
3. Stick to the listed impacts to score.
ex.az: 课本没列糖尿病，答题用课本列出的影响。

cards.en:
Intuition: you beat addiction by putting limits and other good things into your day.

Personal measures:

  • Set time limits; finish important tasks first; use screen-time / rest reminder apps.
  • Have a hobby other than Internet surfing (sport, music, reading).
  • Spend time face to face with family and friends; avoid phubbing.
  • Parents/schools: talk openly, teach healthy use.

Game design to prevent teen addiction (Checkpoint 2.2 Q2):

  • Playtime limit / anti-addiction system that logs out after a set time
  • Break reminders after continuous play
  • Real-name / age verification so limits apply to minors
  • No rewards for continuous log-in (less daily-streak pressure)
  • Spending limits on in-game purchases
cards.zh:
直觉：用限制和其他好活动填满生活来对抗成瘾。

个人：

  • 设定时间限制，先完成重要事情；用屏幕时间/休息提醒 app。
  • 培养上网以外的嗜好。
  • 多和家人朋友面对面相处，避免 phubbing。
  • 家长学校：坦诚沟通、教育。

游戏设计防青少年沉迷：游戏时间上限/防沉迷系统、连续游玩休息提示、实名/年龄验证、取消连续登入奖励、消费上限。

ex.q: Suggest two game-design features to prevent teenage addiction.
ex.a:
1. Anti-addiction system: forces log-out after e.g. 2 hours for players under 18.
2. Real-name verification so the system knows who is a minor.
(Also: break reminders, no streak rewards, spending limits.)
ex.az: 防沉迷系统强制下线；实名验证识别未成年。

ex.q: Why can daily log-in rewards encourage addiction?
ex.a:
1. Players feel they must log in every day or lose the streak.
2. This builds compulsive behaviour.
3. Removing them reduces the pressure.
ex.az: 连续登入奖励令人每天被迫上线。

ex.q: Ivan's parents want to help him cut down phone use. Give two measures.
ex.a:
1. Agree on time limits with a screen-time app.
2. Encourage a hobby like basketball, and family meals with phones away.
ex.az: 设时间限制；培养运动嗜好、吃饭不用手机。

ex.q: "The best way to prevent addiction is to ban all devices at home." Comment.
ex.a:
1. Devices are needed for study and communication.
2. A total ban may cause conflict and is not realistic.
3. Better: time limits + other hobbies + open talk.
ex.az: 全面禁止不实际；应设限、发展嗜好、沟通。

cards.en:
Intuition: phone + snubbing (ignoring). You are with a person, but your eyes are on the phone.

Definition: Phubbing is the act of ignoring someone you are with in person and paying attention to your mobile device instead.

Effect: research shows it affects relationships by making ignored people feel they are excluded or less important. It is one way smartphone addiction harms social life.

Prevention: put the phone away during meals, turn off notifications, agree on "no phone" times with family.

Exam wording: "makes the ignored people feel excluded or less important".
cards.zh:
直觉：phone + snubbing（冷落）。人在身边，眼睛却在手机上。

定义：Phubbing is the act of ignoring someone you are with in person and paying attention to your mobile device instead.

影响：令被冷落的人觉得被排斥或不重要，损害关系。

预防：吃饭时收起手机、关通知、和家人约定"无手机时间"。

ex.q: Four friends at dinner each scroll their own phone and hardly talk. Name the behaviour and its impact.
ex.a:
1. Phubbing.
2. Each friend may feel excluded or less important; the friendship weakens.
ex.az: Phubbing；朋友觉得被排斥，关系变差。

ex.q: Suggest two ways a family can reduce phubbing.
ex.a:
1. A phone basket at meal time.
2. Turn off non-urgent notifications during family time.
ex.az: 吃饭时手机放篮子；关通知。

ex.q: Is replying to an urgent work call during dinner phubbing?
ex.a:
1. Phubbing is ignoring someone to focus on the device.
2. A short, necessary call after excusing yourself is not the habit described.
3. Constant scrolling instead of talking is.
ex.az: 短暂必要通话并道歉不同于持续冷落他人。

ex.q: "Phubbing only harms the person using the phone." What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. The main harm is to the ignored person, who feels excluded.
2. So it harms the relationship, not just the user.
ex.az: 主要伤害被冷落的人和关系。

cards.en:
Intuition: the Internet is a giant open library and loudspeaker. Anyone can read and anyone can speak.

Definition: freedom of information means we are free to express ourselves online and access information distributed by others.

How it changed life (Fig. 2.11):

  • Daily service: e-books from public libraries, news, social media, education.
  • E-commerce: mobile payment, food delivery, ride-hailing, shopping.
  • SOHO (Small Office/Home Office): video conferencing, remote working, cloud collaboration.

Limit: freedom does not justify acts of harming others and society, e.g. fake news, cyberbullying, scams, social engineering, copyright infringement. Abuse leads to legal consequences, including fines and imprisonment.
cards.zh:
直觉：互联网是巨大的开放图书馆加扩音器，人人可以看、可以说。

定义：we are free to express ourselves online and access information distributed by others.

  • 日常服务：公共图书馆电子书、新闻、社交媒体、教育。
  • 电子商贸：流动支付、外卖、网约车、网购。
  • SOHO：视像会议、遥距工作、云端协作。

限制：自由不代表可以伤害他人和社会（假新闻、网络欺凌、诈骗、社交工程、侵犯版权）。滥用可被罚款及监禁。

ex.q: Give one example of freedom of information in each area: daily service, e-commerce, SOHO.
ex.a:
1. Daily service: borrowing an e-book from the public library app.
2. E-commerce: ordering food delivery and paying by mobile payment.
3. SOHO: a video conference while working from home.
ex.az: 电子书；外卖+流动支付；在家视像会议。

ex.q: Emma posts a review saying a restaurant's food was cold. Is this freedom of information?
ex.a:
1. It is her honest opinion based on experience.
2. Yes, she is free to express herself online.
3. It stays legal as long as it is true and not meant to harm.
ex.az: 真实意见，属资讯自由。

ex.q: Why can freedom of information still lead to prison?
ex.a:
1. Freedom is not unlimited.
2. Acts that harm others, e.g. doxxing, defamation, fraud, break laws.
3. Penalties include fines and imprisonment.
ex.az: 伤害他人的行为违法，可罚款监禁。

ex.q: "It's freedom of information, so I can upload the whole new movie for everyone." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Uploading a movie without permission is copyright infringement.
2. Freedom does not justify harming others (the copyright owner).
3. It is illegal.
ex.az: 上传整部电影是侵犯版权，自由不代表可以伤害他人。

cards.t: Pros and cons of freedom of information (Table 2.2)
cards.tz: 资讯自由的优点与缺点
cards.en:
Intuition: "anyone can publish anything" is both the best and the worst thing about the Internet.

ProsCons
Up-to-date informationOut-of-date information
A wide variety of informationLack of quality control
Huge amount of informationOffensive content
Mostly free of chargeFake information
Accessible anytime and anywhereCopyright infringement
Easy exchange of informationInternet addiction
Personal data breach

Why up-to-date AND out-of-date? News is posted instantly, but old pages stay online and are not updated.

Lack of quality control: anyone can publish without editing or checking, so accuracy is not guaranteed.
cards.zh:
直觉："人人都可发布"既是互联网最好也是最坏的地方。

优点缺点
资讯最新资讯过时
种类多缺乏质量控制
数量庞大冒犯性内容
大多免费虚假资讯
随时随地存取侵犯版权
容易交流网络成瘾
个人资料外泄

为何同时"最新"又"过时"？新闻即时发布，但旧网页仍在网上没更新。缺乏质量控制：任何人可发布，没人审核，准确性无保证。

ex.q: Give two pros and two cons of using online forums for homework research.
ex.a:
1. Pros: huge amount and mostly free.
2. Cons: lack of quality control and fake information.
ex.az: 优：量多、免费。缺：缺质控、虚假资讯。

ex.q: Explain "lack of quality control" with an example.
ex.a:
1. No editor checks posts before they go online.
2. E.g. a blog states a wrong formula for kinetic energy.
3. Readers may copy the error.
ex.az: 没人审核，例如博客写错公式。

ex.q: How can the Internet give both up-to-date and out-of-date information?
ex.a:
1. New information is posted instantly (up-to-date).
2. Old pages are not removed or updated, e.g. a 2015 bus timetable.
3. So readers must check the date.
ex.az: 即时发布；旧页没更新，要看日期。

ex.q: A student lists "free of charge" as a con. Why is this marked wrong?
ex.a:
1. Table 2.2 lists mostly free of charge as a pro.
2. A related con would be copyright infringement (free pirated content) or lack of quality control.
ex.az: "免费"是优点；相关缺点是侵权。

cards.tz: 网络欺凌的定义与形式
cards.en:
Intuition: the same bullying as in the playground, but through screens, so it follows you home.

Definition: Cyberbullying is a kind of bullying and harassment that occurs over the Internet. It can happen on messaging apps, social media, games, forums or any platform where people interact. A survey: nearly half of Hong Kong students have experienced it.

Forms in the book:

  • In-game abuse ("Loser!", "Your fault!")
  • Insulting comments on someone's photo in a class group chat
  • Abusive messages ("When will you die?")
  • Reposting someone's photos with teasing comments
  • Doxxing
  • Spreading rumours

Real cases: a Japanese Netflix star died by suicide after months of online abuse (one abuser was fined); K-pop stars Sulli and Goo Hara died in 2019. These led to calls for new laws.
cards.zh:
直觉：和操场欺凌一样，只是透过屏幕，会跟着你回家。

定义：Cyberbullying is a kind of bullying and harassment that occurs over the Internet.可发生在通讯 app、社交媒体、游戏、论坛。调查显示近半香港学生遇过。

形式：游戏中辱骂、班群侮辱照片、恶毒信息、转发照片加嘲笑、起底、散播谣言。

真实个案：日本 Netflix 明星受网暴后自杀（有人被罚款）；2019 年 K-pop 明星 Sulli、具荷拉离世，引发立法讨论。

ex.q: Classmates post a student's photo in the class group chat and add "ugly" comments. Is this cyberbullying?
ex.a:
1. It happens over the Internet (group chat).
2. It is harassment: insulting comments meant to hurt.
3. Yes, cyberbullying.
ex.az: 网上发生、侮辱伤害→是网络欺凌。

ex.q: List three platforms where cyberbullying can happen.
ex.a: Messaging apps, online games, forums (also social media).
ex.az: 通讯 app、网络游戏、论坛。

ex.q: In an online game, a teammate keeps typing "Bad gamer! Your fault!" every match. Which form?
ex.a: In-game abuse, a form of cyberbullying.
ex.az: 游戏中辱骂。

ex.q: "It's only cyberbullying if the bully is a stranger." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Most cases in the book involve classmates (group chats).
2. Anyone, known or anonymous, can cyberbully.
3. The test is harassment over the Internet, not who does it.
ex.az: 同学也可网络欺凌；关键是网上骚扰。

cards.tz: 网络欺凌对心理健康的风险
cards.en:
Key line: Joking does not make people feel bad but bullying does.

Feelings: victims feel lonely, sad, angry and frightened; they may become insecure and isolate themselves.

Consequences: depression, eating disorders; in extreme cases self-harm and suicide.

Why online can be worse than offline:

  • It can happen 24/7, even at home.
  • Content reaches a large audience fast.
  • It stays online and is hard to delete.
  • Bullies can be anonymous.
cards.zh:
重点：Joking does not make people feel bad but bullying does.（玩笑不会令人难受，欺凌会。）

感受：孤单、伤心、愤怒、害怕；变得没安全感、自我孤立。

后果：抑郁、饮食失调，极端时自残、自杀。

为何网上可能更严重：24/7 发生、迅速传给大量观众、长留网上难删除、欺凌者可匿名。

ex.q: Give three feelings and two consequences of being cyberbullied.
ex.a:
1. Feelings: lonely, frightened, angry (also sad, insecure).
2. Consequences: depression, eating disorders.
ex.az: 感受：孤单、害怕、愤怒。后果：抑郁、饮食失调。

ex.q: Give two reasons cyberbullying can be more harmful than face-to-face bullying.
ex.a:
1. 24/7: the victim cannot escape at home.
2. Large audience and stays online: hurtful posts spread and are hard to delete.
ex.az: 24/7 发生；传播广、难删除。

ex.q: A victim stops going to the class party and avoids friends. Which effect is this?
ex.a: Isolating themselves from others, linked to feeling insecure.
ex.az: 自我孤立。

ex.q: "We were only joking, so it is not bullying." How should you respond?
ex.a:
1. Book: joking does not make people feel bad but bullying does.
2. If the target feels hurt, it is bullying, whatever the intent.
ex.az: 若对方受伤害，就是欺凌，不论原意。

cards.en:
Intuition: bullies use what they can find about you, and they feed on reactions. So: share less, react less, record and report.

Prevention: avoid sharing sensitive personal information with people you do not know; set accounts to private (close friends only). Do not participate: don't forward, like or comment.

WhoActions
Victimstell someone you trust; do not respond; block the bullies; collect evidence (screenshots); report to authorities or service providers
Supporterslisten to and stay with the victim; advise them to follow the steps above
Policy and educationanti-cyberbullying policies and laws (Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance, Defamation Ordinance); promote anti-cyberbullying to students and the public
cards.zh:
直觉：欺凌者利用找得到的资料，并喜欢看你反应。所以：少分享、不回应、留证据、举报。

预防：不和陌生人分享敏感个人资料；帐户设私人；不参与（不转发、不讚、不留言）。

谁行动
受害者告诉信任的人；不回应；封锁；截图留证据；向有关当局或服务供应商举报
支持者聆听、陪伴，建议受害者照上面做
政策教育反欺凌政策和法例（私隐条例、诽谤条例）；推广教育

ex.q: Ken receives abusive messages from an anonymous account every night. List his steps in order.
ex.a:
1. Do not respond.
2. Screenshot the messages (evidence).
3. Block the account.
4. Report to the platform / police, and tell a parent or teacher.
ex.az: 不回应→截图→封锁→举报并告诉家长老师。

ex.q: Why should you collect evidence before blocking?
ex.a:
1. After blocking, you may no longer see the messages.
2. Screenshots prove what happened when reporting to the platform, school or police.
ex.az: 封锁后可能看不到信息；截图作举报证据。

ex.q: Your friend is being bullied in a group chat. What can you do as a supporter?
ex.a:
1. Listen and stay with them.
2. Do not like or forward the posts.
3. Advise them to keep evidence, block and report; tell a teacher.
ex.az: 陪伴聆听；不参与；建议留证据、封锁、举报。

ex.q: A victim replies angrily to every bully message to "defend herself". Why is this not advised?
ex.a:
1. Replying gives the bully the reaction they want and escalates the attack.
2. Book advice: do not respond, block, collect evidence, report.
ex.az: 回应会令事件升级；应不回应、封锁、留证据、举报。

frames.en: Do not reply to the bully.
frames.zh: 不回应。

frames.en: Take screenshots with date and username.
frames.zh: 截图，包括日期和帐户名。

frames.en: Block the bully's account.
frames.zh: 封锁。

frames.en: Tell someone you trust; report to the platform or police with evidence.
frames.zh: 告诉信任的人；带证据举报。

cards.en:
Intuition: collecting the scattered pieces of someone's life online (school, phone, photos) and dumping them together in public so others can find them.

Definition: Doxxing (起底) refers to the act of gathering and revealing others' private personal information on the Internet, e.g. on social media and forums: phone number, address, school, photos.

Why it is serious: it is unethical, lets others harass the target offline too, and can lead to fines and imprisonment.

Law: Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance: disclosing someone's personal data without consent, with intent to gain benefit or cause loss.

Exam wording: "gathering and revealing others' private personal information" + "Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance".
cards.zh:
直觉：把某人散在网上的资料（学校、电话、照片）收集起来，公开放在一起让别人找到他。

定义：Doxxing refers to the act of gathering and revealing others' private personal information on the Internet.

为何严重：不道德；令人在现实中也被骚扰；可罚款及监禁。

法例：《个人资料(私隐)条例》：未经同意披露他人资料，意图获益或使其受损。

ex.q: A forum user posts a referee's home address and phone number after a football match, telling fans to "visit him". Name the act and the law.
ex.a:
1. Act: doxxing, gathering and revealing private data.
2. Law: Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance.
3. Penalty: fines and imprisonment.
ex.az: 起底；私隐条例；罚款监禁。

ex.q: Why does doxxing make cyberbullying worse?
ex.a:
1. With a home address or school, bullies can find the target in real life.
2. Harassment moves from online to offline; the victim feels unsafe everywhere.
ex.az: 有地址学校，欺凌可延伸到现实。

ex.q: Is posting your own phone number on your public profile doxxing?
ex.a:
1. Doxxing is revealing others' data without consent.
2. Posting your own is not doxxing, but it is unsafe: others could use it to doxx or scam you.
ex.az: 公开自己资料不是起底，但不安全。

ex.q: "The address was already online somewhere, so reposting it is not doxxing." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Doxxing includes gathering scattered information and revealing it together.
2. Even if each piece was findable, combining and posting it to harm someone is doxxing and can break the law.
ex.az: 收集零散资料再公开以伤害他人仍是起底。

cards.tz: 网络欺凌：旁观者应如何做
cards.en:
Misconception 1: "I only forwarded it; I'm not the bully."
Correct: forwarding, liking or joining spreads the harm and makes you part of the cyberbullying. It may also break the law (reposting defamatory content).

Misconception 2: "The victim should reply and argue back."
Correct: do not respond; replying usually escalates it. Block, keep evidence and report.

Chapter Exercise LQ3: Paul posts "Peter stole my phone! Let's beat him after school!" Jennie should not forward or join because the accusation may be false (defamation) and the post incites violence. She should report it to a teacher and/or tell Peter.
cards.zh:
误解一："我只是转发，不是欺凌者。"
正确：转发、讚好、加入都会扩大伤害，令你成为网络欺凌的一部分，甚至可能违法（转发诽谤内容）。

误解二："受害者应该反驳。"
正确：不回应；封锁、留证据、举报。

LQ3：Paul 发文"Peter 偷了我手机！放学打他！"Jennie 不应转发或参与，因指控可能不实（诽谤）且煽动暴力；应告诉老师和/或通知 Peter。

ex.q: Paul posts "Peter stole my phone! Let's beat him after school!" What should Jennie do and why?
ex.a:
1. Do not forward or reply: the claim may be false (defamation), and it incites violence.
2. Screenshot it.
3. Report to a teacher; warn Peter.
ex.az: 不转发；截图；报告老师、提醒 Peter。

ex.q: Why is "liking" a mean post a problem?
ex.a:
1. Likes push the post to more people (algorithms).
2. It shows support for the bully, encouraging more.
3. So the liker spreads the harm.
ex.az: 讚好令帖子传更广、鼓励欺凌者。

ex.q: A meme mocking a classmate is in your group chat. Give two good bystander actions.
ex.a:
1. Do not forward it; say it's not okay if safe to do so.
2. Support the classmate privately and help them report.
ex.az: 不转发、表态；私下支持并协助举报。

ex.q: "I didn't write it, I just shared it, so I can't be in legal trouble." Is this true?
ex.a:
1. No. Reposting false, damaging content counts as publishing it.
2. It can break the Defamation Ordinance.
ex.az: 转发等于发布，可违反诽谤条例。

cards.tz: 资讯可靠性与事实查证
cards.en:
Intuition: in an information explosion, false posts travel as fast as true ones. Each of us is a filter.

Fact-checking = evaluating the reliability of information before believing or sharing it. Examine its reliability, validity, accuracy, authority, timeliness and bias by comparing various sources.

Rule: Do not share or comment when you are not sure if the information is true.

Slogan (Fig. 2.17): Stop, Think and Check before spreading information.

Example: account "ABC_123" posts typhoon No. 10 signal times "from the Hong Kong Observatory"; it is shared 256 times. Check the official source (Observatory website) first.
cards.zh:
直觉：在资讯爆炸年代，假消息和真消息传得一样快，每个人都是过滤器。

事实查证 = 相信或分享前评估资讯可靠性。透过比较不同来源，检查可靠性、有效性、准确性、权威性、时效性、偏见。

规则：不确定真假时不要分享或评论。

口号：Stop, Think and Check。

例子：帐户"ABC_123"声称天文台发十号风球时间，被转发 256 次，应先查天文台网站。

ex.q: A random account posts that the typhoon No. 10 signal will be raised at 3 pm "according to the Observatory". What should you do?
ex.a:
1. Stop: don't share yet.
2. Think: the account is not official.
3. Check: visit the Hong Kong Observatory website/app.
4. Only share the official information.
ex.az: 停：先不转发。想：非官方帐户。查：天文台网站。

ex.q: Name the six aspects to examine when fact-checking.
ex.a: Reliability, validity, accuracy, authority, timeliness, bias.
ex.az: 可靠性、有效性、准确性、权威性、时效性、偏见。

ex.q: How does "comparing various sources" help?
ex.a:
1. If several independent, trusted sources agree, the information is more likely true.
2. If only one unknown post says it, be careful.
ex.az: 多个可靠来源一致→较可信。

ex.q: "It has been shared 256 times, so it must be true." What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Popularity ≠ truth; fake news often spreads faster.
2. Check the authority of the source, not the share count.
ex.az: 转发多不等于真；看来源权威。

frames.en: "No. 10 signal at 3 pm!" from ABC_123, shared 256 times.
frames.zh: 收到帖子。

frames.en: Do not share or comment yet.
frames.zh: 先不分享。

frames.en: Who posted it? Anonymous, no date, emotional tone?
frames.zh: 谁发？匿名？无日期？

frames.en: Compare with the official source: Observatory website.
frames.zh: 对照官方来源。

frames.en: Official site disagrees → it is fake → do not share; you may report it.
frames.zh: 官方不同→假消息→不转发。

cards.en:
Intuition: treat information like a used car: check who sells it, when it was made, and whether the seller is honest.

CriterionQuestion to ask
ReliabilityIs the source trustworthy (official, reputable)?
ValidityIs it logical and supported by evidence?
AccuracyAre facts, numbers, quotes correct? Do other sources agree?
AuthorityWho is the author/organisation? An expert?
TimelinessWhen was it published/updated? Out of date?
BiasOne-sided, an advert, trying to make you angry?

Method: compare various sources.

Red flags: anonymous account, no date, emotional headline, "forward to everyone", too good to be true (e.g. a $500 coupon bug).
cards.zh:
直觉：像买二手车：看谁卖、几时造、卖家是否诚实。

准则要问
Reliability 可靠性来源可信吗？
Validity 有效性合逻辑、有证据吗？
Accuracy 准确性数字引述正确？其他来源一致？
Authority 权威性作者是谁？专家吗？
Timeliness 时效性何时发布/更新？
Bias 偏见片面？广告？煽动情绪？

方法：比较多个来源。警号：匿名、无日期、煽情标题、"请转发"、好得难以置信。

ex.q: A health website selling vitamin pills says "our pills cure flu in 1 day". Which criteria fail?
ex.a:
1. Bias: the site sells the product (advert).
2. Validity: no evidence/studies given.
3. Authority: not a medical body. Compare with the Department of Health.
ex.az: 偏见（卖产品）、有效性（无证据）、权威性（非医学机构）。

ex.q: A student uses a 2012 article for "latest smartphone sales". Which criterion fails?
ex.a: Timeliness: the data is out of date.
ex.az: 时效性。

ex.q: Which source is more authoritative for a vaccine fact: (A) Centre for Health Protection (B) a celebrity's post? Why?
ex.a:
1. A.
2. It is an official expert organisation (authority, reliability).
ex.az: A，官方专家机构。

ex.q: "The article is well written with nice pictures, so it is reliable." Comment.
ex.a:
1. Design quality says nothing about truth.
2. Check who wrote it, when, evidence, bias and compare sources.
ex.az: 排版漂亮不代表可靠，要查作者、日期、证据。

cards.en:
Intuition: the harm grows with how many people believe it.

ScaleExample of harm
Youwrong info in an assignment → lower score
Your dayfalse weather info → ruins your plan
Another personfake news harming someone's image → hurt feelings, damaged reputation
Societymisinformation causing social chaos → may endanger national security

Case (2020): false rumours about supply shortages spread on instant messaging and social media and triggered toilet paper and dry grocery panic buying in Hong Kong. The government took measures to stop misinformation.

Exam wording: "Everyone has the responsibility to think critically before spreading any information."
cards.zh:
直觉：相信的人越多，伤害越大。

层面例子
自己功课用错资料→分数低
日常假天气资讯→打乱计划
他人假新闻损形象→伤害感受、名誉
社会社会混乱→甚至危害国家安全

2020 个案：物资短缺谣言在通讯软件和社交媒体流传，引发抢购厕纸和干货。

考试写法：Everyone has the responsibility to think critically before spreading any information.

ex.q: Explain how a rumour led to panic buying in 2020.
ex.a:
1. Rumour: toilet paper will run out (production stopped, imports limited).
2. Spread fast via instant messages and social media.
3. People rushed to buy → shelves empty → the rumour seemed "true" → more panic.
4. Result: social chaos.
ex.az: 谣言经通讯软件传播→抢购→货架空→更恐慌。

ex.q: Give one personal-level and one society-level impact of misinformation.
ex.a:
1. Personal: an assignment with wrong facts gets a lower score.
2. Society: a fake post about a bank collapsing causes a bank run (social chaos).
ex.az: 个人：功课扣分。社会：假消息引发挤提。

ex.q: A false post says a teacher hit a student. It is shared widely. What impacts follow?
ex.a:
1. The teacher's image and reputation are damaged; hurt feelings.
2. Sharers may break the Defamation Ordinance.
ex.az: 损害老师名誉；转发者可能违诽谤条例。

ex.q: "Sharing a rumour is harmless if I add 'not sure if true'." Comment.
ex.a:
1. The post still spreads the rumour to more people.
2. Book rule: do not share when you are not sure; check first.
ex.az: 加"未证实"仍在散播；不确定就不要分享。

cards.tz: 法律后果：《个人资料(私隐)条例》
cards.en:
Intuition: the Basic Law protects freedom of speech, but laws stop that freedom from being used to hurt people (Table 2.3).

Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance (個人資料(私隱)條例):

  • Definition: disclosing someone's personal data without their agreement with the intention to gain benefit or cause loss to that person.
  • Penalties: fines and imprisonment.
  • Applicable cases: doxxing, e.g. disclosing someone's mobile number; creating an account with someone's photos and personal information without permission.

Personal data = data that can identify a person: name, ID number, phone number, address, photos.
cards.zh:
直觉：《基本法》保障言论自由，但法例防止有人用自由伤人。

《个人资料(私隐)条例》：

  • 定义：未经同意披露他人个人资料，意图获益或令对方受损。
  • 罚则：罚款及监禁。
  • 适用：起底（公开别人手机号码）；未经许可用别人照片和资料开帐户。

个人资料：可识别个人的资料，如姓名、身份证号、电话、地址、照片。

ex.q: Someone creates an Instagram account using Amy's photos and name without permission. Which law?
ex.a:
1. Uses Amy's personal data without agreement.
2. Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance.
3. Penalty: fines and imprisonment.
ex.az: 私隐条例。

ex.q: Which are personal data? (1) HKID number (2) favourite colour (3) home address (4) a clear photo of a face
ex.a:
1. (1) yes (2) no, cannot identify a person (3) yes (4) yes.
Answer: (1), (3), (4).

ex.q: George posts Amy's phone number after an argument so others can call her. Explain the offence.
ex.a:
1. Disclosed Amy's personal data without agreement.
2. Intention: to cause loss/harm (harassment).
3. Breaks the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance.
ex.az: 未经同意公开电话，意图伤害→违私隐条例。

ex.q: "Freedom of speech in the Basic Law means I can post anyone's address." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. The Basic Law protects free speech, but other laws restrict abuse.
2. Posting someone's address without consent can break the Privacy Ordinance.
ex.az: 言论自由受其他法例限制；公开地址违私隐条例。

cards.t: Legal consequences: Defamation and Theft Ordinances
cards.tz: 法律后果：《诽谤条例》与《盗窃罪条例》
cards.en:
Intuition: lies that hurt someone's name → Defamation. Using information to get money → Theft (blackmail, fraud).

Defamation Ordinance 誹謗條例Theft Ordinance 盜竊罪條例
DefinitionPublishing information that harms someone's reputationBlackmail: demanding benefit for not disclosing someone's information.
Fraud: using false personal information to obtain property
PenaltiesFines and imprisonmentImprisonment
CasesReposting fake news that harms a person/party; spreading false information about someone you hateBlackmail (勒索): demand money for not leaking data. Fraud (欺詐): fake profiles to steal money

Example: George posts Amy's number and photos (Privacy) and claims falsely that she shoplifted (Defamation). Not copyright.

Exam wording: name the ordinance + the matching definition phrase.
cards.zh:
直觉：说谎损人名誉→诽谤；用资料来拿钱→盗窃罪（勒索、欺诈）。

诽谤条例盗窃罪条例
定义发布损害他人名誉的资讯勒索：要求利益以换取不公开资料。欺诈：用虚假个人资料骗取财物
罚则罚款及监禁监禁
例子转发损人名誉的假新闻勒索要钱；假帐户骗钱

例：George 公开 Amy 电话照片（私隐），并诬告她偷窃（诽谤）。

ex.q: Someone messages Leo: "Pay $5,000 or I'll post your private chats." Which law?
ex.a:
1. Demanding money for not disclosing information = blackmail.
2. Theft Ordinance; penalty: imprisonment.
ex.az: 勒索→盗窃罪条例。

ex.q: A scammer pretends to be a bank officer with a fake profile and gets $20,000. Which offence?
ex.a:
1. Uses false personal information to obtain property = fraud.
2. Theft Ordinance.
ex.az: 欺诈→盗窃罪条例。

ex.q: George posts Amy's phone number and a false claim that she shoplifted. Which ordinances?
ex.a:
1. Phone number without consent → Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance.
2. False claim harming reputation → Defamation Ordinance.
3. Not copyright (nothing copied).
ex.az: 私隐条例 + 诽谤条例。

ex.q: "Posting a TRUE but embarrassing photo of a classmate is defamation." Is this right?
ex.a:
1. Defamation is about false information that harms reputation.
2. A true photo posted without consent is more a privacy / cyberbullying issue.
3. Pick the law that fits the facts.
ex.az: 诽谤针对不实内容；真实照片未经同意是私隐/欺凌问题。

cards.en:
Intuition: scammers don't hack computers, they hack people: greed, fear, kindness.

Social engineering = tricking people into giving information or money (Core C section 5.3). Scamming is an abuse of freedom of information.

Checkpoint example: George posts "I found a bug on a shopping site! Got a $500 coupon. DM me for the method!" Amy does not repost because:

  1. It may be a scam, as George's identity is unknown.
  2. It may cause a huge loss to the shopping site.
  3. It is illegal to steal coupons without authority.

Exercise example: an online friend "Amy" asks Andy to lend money for tuition. His classmate disagrees: Amy may tell lies and it may be fraud (Theft Ordinance).
cards.zh:
直觉：骗徒不是骇入电脑，而是"骇入人心"：利用贪心、恐惧、善心。

社交工程 = 欺骗他人交出资料或金钱。

例子：George 声称发现购物网站漏洞拿到 $500 优惠券，叫人私讯。Amy 不转发因为：1. 身份不明，可能是骗局；2. 可令网站巨大损失；3. 未经授权取优惠券违法。

另一例：网友"Amy"向 Andy 借学费——可能说谎，可能是欺诈。

ex.q: Give three reasons not to repost George's "$500 coupon bug" post.
ex.a:
1. May be a scam: George's identity is unknown; the DM may ask for your account details.
2. Huge loss to the shopping site.
3. Illegal to take coupons without authority.
ex.az: 可能骗局；令网站损失；未经授权违法。

ex.q: An online friend you've never met asks to borrow $3,000 for tuition. What should you do?
ex.a:
1. You cannot verify who they are.
2. It may be fraud.
3. Do not send money; tell a parent; report the account if suspicious.
ex.az: 无法核实身份，可能欺诈；不借钱、告诉家长。

ex.q: A message says "Your parcel is held. Click this link and pay $15 in 24 hours." Which trick is used?
ex.a:
1. Urgency/fear (24 hours).
2. Small fee to seem harmless; link steals card data.
3. Social engineering → check with the official courier site.
ex.az: 利用急迫和恐惧；查官方网站。

ex.q: "I'll just DM to see the method; asking is safe." Why is this risky?
ex.a:
1. The scammer starts a private chat where they can ask for passwords or payment and pressure you.
2. Safer: ignore and report the post.
ex.az: 私讯给骗徒机会索取资料；应忽略并举报。

cards.t: Protecting personal data on social media
cards.tz: 在社交媒体保护个人资料
cards.en:
Intuition: most leaks are not hacks; they are things we posted ourselves.

  • Set the account to private and only allow close friends to see posts.
  • Do not post sensitive data: phone, address, school, ID, real-time location.
  • Think before posting photos; once online they can be reposted to forums.
  • Check each app's privacy settings regularly.

Checkpoint: Eva posted funny-face selfies on a public account; they were reposted to a forum with teasing comments. Best prevention: set her account to private and only allow close friends to see it. (Not: stop taking selfies, quit the Internet, or comment on the forum asking people to stop.)
cards.zh:
直觉：大部分外泄不是被黑客入侵，而是自己发布的。

  • 帐户设私人，只让好友看。
  • 不发敏感资料：电话、地址、学校、身份证、实时位置。
  • 发照片前三思，一上网就可被转发。
  • 定期检查私隐设定。

例子：Eva 在公开帐户发鬼脸自拍，被转到论坛嘲笑。最佳预防：设为私人，只让好友看（不是不自拍、不上网，或在论坛留言叫人停止）。

ex.q: Eva's public selfies were reposted to a forum. Best prevention?
ex.a:
1. Root cause: account is public.
2. Fix: set the account to private, only close friends can see.
3. Other options (stop selfies, quit Internet) are unrealistic.
ex.az: 帐户设私人，只让好友看。

ex.q: A student's post shows her school uniform badge and "at home now 🏠" with location tag. What data is leaked?
ex.a:
1. School (badge).
2. Home location (tag + text).
3. Fix: remove location tags; avoid showing badges.
ex.az: 泄露学校和住址；关位置标签。

ex.q: Give two privacy settings to check on a new app.
ex.a:
1. Who can see my posts (public/friends/private).
2. Location sharing on/off.
ex.az: 谁可看帖子；位置分享。

ex.q: "I'll comment on the forum asking people to delete my photo; that prevents leakage." Comment.
ex.a:
1. The photo is already leaked; asking may attract more attention.
2. It does not prevent anything.
3. Prevention = private account; after leaking: report to the forum and keep evidence.
ex.az: 已外泄，留言不是预防；应设私人帐户，事后向论坛举报。

cards.t: Digital equity and Internet penetration in Hong Kong
cards.tz: 数码平等与香港互联网普及率
cards.en:
Intuition: today, much of life (banking, booking, school) is online. If you cannot get online, you are partly locked out of society.

Definition: Digital equity refers to the condition in which people have equitable access to technology to participate in modern society.

Hong Kong (OGCIO 2021):

ItemRate
Household Internet penetration94%
Smartphone penetration92.1%
Personal computer75.3%
Mobile subscriber penetration292% (more than 2 subscriptions per person)
Usage of the Internet92%

High rates, but digital equity issues still exist locally and globally.
cards.zh:
直觉：今天很多生活（银行、预约、上学）都在网上；上不了网，就被社会部分排斥。

定义：Digital equity refers to the condition in which people have equitable access to technology to participate in modern society.

香港 (OGCIO 2021)：住户上网 94%、智能手机 92.1%、个人电脑 75.3%、流动电话用户 292%（每人多于两个）、互联网使用 92%。

普及率高，但本地和全球仍有数码平等问题。

ex.q: How can mobile subscriber penetration be 292%?
ex.a:
1. Penetration = subscriptions ÷ population × 100%.
2. 292% means about 2.92 subscriptions per person.
3. Many people have two phones, a tablet SIM, data SIMs, etc.
ex.az: 292% ≈ 每人 2.92 个用户号码，很多人有多张卡。

ex.q: A city has 2,000,000 households; 1,880,000 have Internet. Find the household penetration rate.
Explain digital equity in your own words with an example.
ex.a:
1. Everyone should have fair access to technology to take part in society.
2. E.g. a student from a poor family gets a subsidised laptop and Internet so she can join online lessons like classmates.
ex.az: 人人公平使用科技；如资助贫困学生电脑上网。

ex.q: "Penetration is over 90%, so Hong Kong has full digital equity." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. The remaining ~6-8% are often the elderly, low-income or disabled.
2. Having access ≠ having skills or quality access.
3. Digital equity issues still exist.
ex.az: 剩下的人多是弱势；有网络不等于有技能，仍有问题。

cards.tz: 数码隔阂的意思与范畴
cards.en:
Intuition: picture two groups on either side of a river; the bridge is technology. The digital divide is how wide that river is.

Definition: Digital divide describes the gap between individuals or groups of people in terms of:

Hardware and softwareInternet connectionICT skills and literacy
Necessary tools
Quality
Localisation		Broadband and mobile network
Stability
Data transfer speed		Obtaining information
Processing information and creating new ideas
Lifelong learning

Impact: people on the wrong side become increasingly isolated from necessary daily services and less competitive in the job market.

Example: shops moving online (e.g. a clothing chain closed all HK stores in 2020) can leave people with low computer literacy unable to shop.
cards.zh:
直觉：两群人隔着一条河，桥是科技。数码隔阂就是河有多宽。

定义：个人或群体之间在以下方面的差距：

硬件软件网络连接ICT 技能与素养
必要工具、质量、本地化宽频/流动网络、稳定性、速度取得资讯、处理资讯与创新、终身学习

影响：越来越与日常必要服务隔绝，就业竞争力下降。

ex.q: Name the three aspects of the digital divide with one example each.
ex.a:
1. Hardware and software: a family shares one old phone.
2. Internet connection: a village has slow, unstable network.
3. ICT skills and literacy: a retiree cannot use online banking.
ex.az: 硬软件：共用旧手机；网络：村落网络慢；技能：不会网上银行。

ex.q: Why does the digital divide make people less competitive in the job market?
ex.a:
1. Many jobs need digital skills (email, spreadsheets, online applications).
2. Without them, people cannot apply or perform → fewer opportunities.
ex.az: 工作需要数码技能，欠缺者机会少。

ex.q: A shopping mall's shops close and move online. Who is affected and how?
ex.a:
1. People with low computer literacy (e.g. elderly).
2. They lose a way to buy daily goods → isolated from daily services.
ex.az: 电脑能力低者难以购物，被日常服务隔绝。

ex.q: A student says digital divide is "only about whether you have the Internet". What is missing?
ex.a:
1. Also hardware/software quality and localisation.
2. Also ICT skills and literacy.
3. Three aspects, not one.
ex.az: 还有硬软件和技能，共三方面。

cards.t: Causes: demographic factors (age, gender, race, ethnicity)
cards.en:
Intuition: who you are (your age, gender, background) can shape how much tech you get to learn.

Aging problem: the elderly know less about PCs and are less likely to have smartphones, so they use online purchase and mobile payment much less. (OGCIO 2021: PC skills young/middle-aged 96% vs elderly 49%; smartphone 98% vs 68%.)

Gender gap: females show less interest and confidence in STEM because of the stereotypical belief that only boys have the inborn talent for STEM. Prefer STEM at university: female 14%, male 40% (EdUHK 2018). Women in big tech (2020): Apple total 34% / tech 24%; Google 33% / 26%.

Hedy Lamarr's frequency hopping idea inspired Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and GPS: proof that talent is not limited by gender.
cards.zh:
直觉：你的年龄、性别、背景会影响你学到多少科技。

人口老化：长者较少懂电脑、较少有智能手机，少用网购和流动支付。（2021：电脑技能 96% 对 49%；智能手机 98% 对 68%。）

性别差距：因为"只有男孩有 STEM 天分"的刻板印象，女性对 STEM 兴趣和信心较低。大学想读 STEM：女 14%、男 40%。2020 苹果女性占 34%（技术 24%），Google 33%（26%）。

Hedy Lamarr 的跳频技术启发了 Wi-Fi、蓝牙、GPS。

ex.q: Using the OGCIO data, how much bigger is the PC-skill rate of young people than the elderly?
ex.a:
1. 96% − 49% = 47 percentage points.
2. Ratio: 96 ÷ 49 ≈ 1.96 times.

ex.q: Explain why the elderly use mobile payment less.
ex.a:
1. Fewer own smartphones (68% vs 98%).
2. Less knowledge/confidence with apps; worry about scams.
3. So they keep using cash → divide in daily services.
ex.az: 较少有智能手机、缺乏知识信心。

ex.q: How does a stereotype cause a gender digital divide?
ex.a:
1. Belief: only boys have STEM talent.
2. Girls get less encouragement → less interest and confidence.
3. Fewer choose STEM (14% vs 40%) → fewer women in tech jobs.
ex.az: 刻板印象→女生缺信心→少读 STEM→科技业女性少。

ex.q: "Fewer women work in tech because women are naturally worse at it." Comment.
ex.a:
1. The book says the cause is a stereotypical belief, not ability.
2. Example: Hedy Lamarr's frequency hopping.
3. The gap comes from interest and confidence shaped by society.
ex.az: 原因是刻板印象而非能力，例如 Hedy Lamarr。

cards.en:
Intuition: money, schooling and having a job all decide how much tech you can buy and learn.

FactorWhyOGCIO 2021 data
Educationsecondary/higher education → more chances to learn advanced techPC skills: primary 53%, secondary 96%, post-secondary 99%. Smartphone: 68% / 97% / 99%
Household incomehigh-speed Internet, high-end devices and PCs are less affordable to low-income householdsInternet: <$10,000 72% vs ≥$10,000 99%. PC: 35% vs 85%
Work statuseconomically active people learn and use new tech at work; may feel left out after retirementPC skills 97% vs 53%; smartphone 99% vs 71%
cards.zh:
直觉：钱、教育程度、有没有工作，决定你能买和学多少科技。

因素原因2021 数据
教育中学或以上较多机会学先进科技电脑技能：小学 53%、中学 96%、专上 99%
住户收入低收入家庭负担不起高速网络、高端装置上网：<$10,000 72%，≥$10,000 99%；电脑 35% 对 85%
工作状况从事经济活动者在工作中学新科技；退休后可能落后电脑技能 97% 对 53%

ex.q: Household income under $10,000: PC ownership 35%; at or above: 85%. Out of 1,000 low-income homes, how many have no PC?
Explain why work status affects ICT skills.
ex.a:
1. Workers use email, spreadsheets, apps at work → keep learning.
2. Retired people lose this daily practice and may feel left out.
ex.az: 在职者每天用科技；退休后缺练习而落后。

ex.q: A low-income student shares one phone with two siblings for online lessons. Which factor and aspect?
ex.a:
1. Factor: household income (socioeconomic status).
2. Aspect: hardware (necessary tools).
ex.az: 住户收入；硬件方面。

ex.q: A student says "education level doesn't matter since everyone in HK has smartphones." Use data to correct.
ex.a:
1. Smartphone ownership: primary education 68% vs post-secondary 99%.
2. PC skills: 53% vs 99%.
3. Education clearly matters.
ex.az: 数据：小学程度 68% 对专上 99%，教育有影响。

cards.en:
Intuition: laying cables is expensive; companies lay them where there are many customers.

Urban vs rural: cities have more people and customers → infrastructure (free Wi-Fi, broadband, mobile network) already exists and only needs upgrading. Countryside faces higher prices because of high infrastructure cost and less price competition.

Developing vs developed countries: gap due to national economies and education conditions.

Language: about 7,000 languages/dialects, but only about 12 are widely used online; website content: English 61%, Chinese 1.4%. Minority-language speakers face less localised and translated content and may only use tech in a second language.
cards.zh:
直觉：铺线很贵，公司只会在客人多的地方铺。

城乡：城市人多，基建已有只需升级；乡郊因基建成本高、价格竞争少，价格较高。

发展中与已发展国家：差距源于国家经济和教育条件。

语言：约 7000 种语言方言，网上只有约 12 种常用；网站内容英文 61%、中文 1.4%。少数语言使用者面对较少本地化和翻译内容。

ex.q: Why is broadband often more expensive in rural areas?
ex.a:
1. Few customers spread over a large area → high infrastructure cost per user.
2. Few providers → less price competition.
3. So prices are higher.
ex.az: 基建成本高、竞争少→价格高。

ex.q: A Nepali-speaking elder in Hong Kong struggles with government apps. Which cause?
ex.a:
1. Language: less localised and translated content.
2. She must use tech in a second language → harder to use services.
ex.az: 语言：缺本地化内容。

ex.q: Compare the share of web content in English and Chinese.
ex.a:
1. English 61%, Chinese 1.4%.
2. 61 ÷ 1.4 ≈ 44 times more English content.

ex.q: "The digital divide between countries is only due to geography (mountains, distance)." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. The book names national economies and education conditions as the main reasons between countries.
2. Physical distance matters more for urban vs rural.
ex.az: 国家间差距主要因经济和教育条件。

cards.en:
Intuition: most apps are designed for people who can see, hear and use both hands. Others hit walls.

Types: visual impairment (視覺障礙), hearing impairment (聽覺障礙), physical disability (肢體殘障), cognitive impairment (認知障礙).

Two causes:

  • Website and software accessibility: only a few private websites and new technologies consider accessibility → a barrier. (HK: 100% of government websites/apps accessible, 2018.)
  • Extra cost for assistive technology: besides normal device and Internet costs, disabled users need assistive devices/software, often expensive, and still limited by content design.

Example: Professor Stephen Hawking used muscle sensors and special software (ACAT, later open source) to control a computer and speak.
cards.zh:
直觉：大部分 app 假设用户看得见、听得到、能用双手，其他人就会碰壁。

类型：视觉障碍、听觉障碍、肢体残障、认知障碍。

  • 网站软件无障碍：只有少数私人网站和新科技考虑无障碍→形成障碍。（香港政府网站 app 2018 年 100% 无障碍。）
  • 辅助科技额外成本：除一般开支外还要买辅助装置/软件，往往昂贵。

例：霍金用肌肉感应器和软件 (ACAT) 控制电脑说话。

ex.q: Give the two reasons people with disabilities face a digital divide.
ex.a:
1. Lack of accessibility in private websites and new tech.
2. Extra cost of assistive technology.
ex.az: 缺乏无障碍设计；辅助科技额外成本。

ex.q: A shopping app has image-only buttons with no text. Who is affected and why?
ex.a:
1. Visually impaired users using screen readers.
2. The screen reader has no text to read → they cannot shop.
3. Fix: add alt text / labels.
ex.az: 视障者；读屏软件读不到；加替代文字。

ex.q: How did Stephen Hawking use technology to communicate?
ex.a:
1. A muscle sensor on his cheek detected small movements.
2. Software (ACAT) turned these into selections → text → speech.
ex.az: 肌肉感应器+软件转成文字和语音。

ex.q: "Government sites are 100% accessible, so disabled people face no digital divide in HK." Comment.
ex.a:
1. That covers only government sites.
2. Many private websites/apps are not accessible.
3. And cost of assistive tech remains.
ex.az: 只限政府网站；私人网站和成本问题仍在。

cards.en:
Intuition: if nobody acts, the gap only grows, because tech keeps moving forward. The government can pay for what individuals cannot.

HK spent about HK$10,721 million on ICT in 2019-2020 (OGCIO).

  • Provide free Wi-Fi hotspots and IT facilities in public places.
  • Subsidise needy students from low-income families for hardware, software and Internet.
  • Fund schools' IT and Wi-Fi infrastructure.
  • Expand fibre-based network to old buildings and remote areas (5G).
  • Fund accessible apps and websites.
  • Recognition schemes to encourage digital inclusion.

Exam wording: match measure → cause, e.g. "subsidise needy students" targets household income.
cards.zh:
直觉：科技不断前进，没人行动差距只会扩大。政府可以支付个人负担不起的东西。

2019-2020 年香港 ICT 开支约 107.21 亿港元。

  • 公共地方免费 Wi-Fi和 IT 设施。
  • 资助低收入家庭学生购买硬软件和上网。
  • 资助学校 IT 和 Wi-Fi 基建。
  • 把光纤网络扩展到旧楼和偏远地区。
  • 资助开发无障碍 app 和网站。
  • 嘉许计划鼓励数码共融。

考试写法：措施要对应成因。

ex.q: Match each measure to the cause it targets: (a) fibre to remote villages (b) subsidy for needy students (c) funding accessible apps
ex.a:
(a) geographical location
(b) household income
(c) disability
ex.az: (a) 地理 (b) 收入 (c) 残疾。

ex.q: How do free Wi-Fi hotspots help bridge the divide?
ex.a:
1. People who cannot afford home broadband/data can still get online.
2. Access to government services, job search, study.
ex.az: 负担不起上网的人也能使用。

ex.q: Suggest a government measure for students who cannot join online lessons.
ex.a:
1. Subsidise a laptop/tablet and mobile data.
2. Fund the school to lend devices and improve Wi-Fi.
ex.az: 资助电脑和数据；资助学校借出装置。

ex.q: "Making all government services online-only bridges the divide." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. It widens the gap for the elderly and low-income.
2. Good measures keep alternatives (counter, phone) plus support and training.
ex.az: 只网上会扩大隔阂；要保留其他途径。

cards.en:
Intuition: giving someone a phone does not help if they cannot use it. Skills are the third aspect of the divide.

  • Support for parenting in the digital age (parenting apps, IT training).
  • Prepare teachers for online teaching and tech skills.
  • Internet learning support programmes for people lacking basic IT skills.

Elderly: Elderly IT Learning Portal (share skills online); ICT Outreach Programme (teach basic IT skills). An advanced ICT course does not fit their basic-skill gap.

Gender: Girls Go Tech (The Women's Foundation): workshops (hackathon, AI experience) and career talks for underprivileged girls → builds interest and confidence, breaks stereotypes.
cards.zh:
直觉：给人手机但他不会用，也帮不了。技能是数码隔阂第三方面。

  • 数码时代亲职支援。
  • 培训教师网上教学。
  • 为缺乏基本 IT 技能者设上网学习支援计划。

长者：长者 IT 学习平台；ICT 外展计划教基本技能（不是进阶课程）。

性别：Girls Go Tech：工作坊和职业讲座，建立兴趣和信心，打破刻板印象。

ex.q: Suggest two education measures for elderly people.
ex.a:
1. ICT Outreach Programme: volunteers teach basic phone skills at elderly centres.
2. Elderly IT Learning Portal: short videos on using e-payment.
ex.az: 外展计划；长者学习平台。

ex.q: How does Girls Go Tech reduce the gender gap?
ex.a:
1. Workshops let girls try tech hands-on → interest.
2. Success and role models → confidence.
3. Career talks break the stereotype that only boys do STEM.
ex.az: 动手→兴趣；成功→信心；讲座打破刻板印象。

ex.q: Why train teachers as part of bridging the divide?
ex.a:
1. Students learn IT skills from teachers.
2. Teachers must be ready for online teaching so every student gets quality IT education.
ex.az: 教师要懂网上教学，学生才得到优质教育。

ex.q: A centre offers an "Advanced Python for AI" course to help elderly residents use mobile banking. Comment.
ex.a:
1. The elderly's gap is basic skills.
2. An advanced course does not match.
3. Better: a basic course on smartphones and mobile payment.
ex.az: 长者需要基本技能，进阶课程不对题。

cards.tz: 为残疾人士设计的辅助科技
cards.en:
Intuition: glasses help weak eyes; assistive tech does the same for computers.

Definition: Assistive technology is any device, software, or equipment designed to overcome the physical barrier. It allows the disabled to browse the Internet and use other digital devices equally.

TechnologyHow it helpsFor
Braille display 點字顯示器shows output as braille characters by raising dotsvisually impaired
Screen reader / Voice-over, digital assistantscreen content described in speech; control by voice; type with speech-to-textvisually / physically impaired
Video call and live captioncamera lets users sign; captions show speech as texthearing impaired
Live transcribespeech → text in real time by speech recognitionhearing impaired
Closed captioningsubtitles with dialogue and non-speech audio (e.g. [door slams])hearing impaired
cards.zh:
直觉：眼镜帮视力差的人；辅助科技帮人用电脑。

定义：Assistive technology is any device, software, or equipment designed to overcome the physical barrier.让残疾人士平等地上网和使用数码装置。

科技作用对象
点字显示器升起圆点显示点字视障
读屏/Voice-over、数码助理把屏幕内容读出；声控；语音转文字视障/肢体
视像通话+实时字幕用手语；字幕显示说话听障
Live transcribe实时语音转文字听障
Closed captioning字幕含对白和非对白声音听障

ex.q: Suggest assistive technology for a blind student reading a web page.
ex.a:
1. Screen reader: reads text aloud.
2. Braille display: shows the text as raised dots under the fingers.
ex.az: 读屏软件；点字显示器。

ex.q: What is the difference between live transcribe and closed captioning?
ex.a:
1. Live transcribe: converts live speech around you (a conversation) to text in real time.
2. Closed captioning: subtitles for a video, including non-speech sounds.
ex.az: 实时转写现场说话；字幕配合影片并含非对白声音。

ex.q: A user with no use of his hands wants to send a message. What helps?
ex.a: Digital assistant / voice control with speech-to-text: "Send a message to Mum: I'm home."
ex.az: 数码助理声控+语音转文字。

ex.q: "Closed captions are just the same as normal subtitles." What is missing?
ex.a:
1. Closed captions also show non-speech audio information, e.g. [phone ringing], [music].
2. Hearing-impaired viewers need this to follow the story.
ex.az: 还包括非对白声音资讯。

demo.title: How a screen reader helps a blind user

frames.en: The app shows buttons and text.
frames.zh: 页面载入。

frames.en: User taps an item; the screen reader reads it aloud: "Pay button".
frames.zh: 单击，读出"Pay button"。

frames.en: Double tap to select / activate.
frames.zh: 双击选择。

frames.en: If an image button has no alt text, it only says "button": the user is stuck.
frames.zh: 没有替代文字就只读"button"。

cards.en:
Intuition: build the content so everyone can use it from the start, instead of fixing it later.

The HK government issued an accessibility handbook for web/app design; GovHK provides ethnic minority languages.

  • Multi-language: ethnic minorities use services without knowing Chinese or English (Hindi, Bahasa Indonesia, Nepali...).
  • High contrast version: for people with colour blindness (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia) who cannot tell similar colours apart.
  • Alternative text (alt text): describes an image in text ("The sun is above a mountain") so screen readers can read it.

Other features: text size buttons (A A A), sitemap, mobile version, language switch, search; video sites: captions, playback speed, audio description, keyboard shortcuts.

Exam wording: feature + who it helps + how.
cards.zh:
直觉：一开始就设计成人人可用，而不是事后补救。

政府发出无障碍手册；GovHK 提供少数族裔语言。

  • 多语言：少数族裔不懂中英文也可使用。
  • 高对比版本：帮助色盲人士分辨元素。
  • 替代文字 (alt text)：用文字描述图片，让读屏软件读出。

其他：字体大小按钮、网站地图、流动版、语言切换、搜寻；影片：字幕、播放速度、口述影像、键盘快捷键。

ex.q: Write suitable alt text for a photo of a red bus at a stop with passengers boarding.
ex.a:
1. Describe what matters, short and clear.
2. alt="Passengers boarding a red bus at a bus stop"
3. A screen reader reads this aloud.
ex.az: alt="乘客在巴士站登上红色巴士"。

ex.q: A website uses green text on a red background. Who has trouble and what fixes it?
ex.a:
1. People with colour blindness (red-green, e.g. deuteranopia).
2. Provide a high contrast version (e.g. black on white).
ex.az: 色盲人士；高对比版本。

ex.q: How does a multi-language website help digital equity?
ex.a:
1. Ethnic minorities can read services in their own language.
2. They are no longer blocked by not knowing Chinese/English.
ex.az: 少数族裔可用母语使用服务。

ex.q: A designer writes alt="image1.jpg" for every picture. What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. The screen reader reads "image1.jpg", which tells the user nothing.
2. Alt text must describe the image content.
ex.az: 替代文字要描述内容，不是档名。

cards.tz: 智能手机的无障碍功能
cards.en:
Intuition: your own phone already has assistive tech hidden in Settings → Accessibility.

  • Screen reader / Voice-over: describes the screen in speech; tap to hear an option, double tap to select.
  • Live transcribe: real-time speech-to-text.
  • Closed captioning: subtitles automatically shown with videos.
  • Digital assistant: voice commands for calls, schedules, searching.

Advantages of a live transcription app (Checkpoint 2.5):

  1. Makes communication between hearing impaired people and the world easier.
  2. Jots notes in meetings and lessons automatically.
  3. Reduces RSI by reducing keyboard use.

It narrows (not widens) the digital divide.

For a 70-year-old with a tablet: make the font bigger and install a simple and clean launcher.
cards.zh:
直觉：你的手机设定→辅助使用已经有辅助科技。

  • 读屏/Voice-over：单击听选项，双击选择。
  • Live transcribe：实时语音转文字。
  • 字幕：影片自动显示字幕。
  • 数码助理：声控打电话、行事历、搜寻。

实时转写 app 好处：1. 方便听障人士与外界沟通；2. 会议上课自动做笔记；3. 少打字减少 RSI。它缩窄数码隔阂。

70 岁长者用平板：放大字体，安装简洁的启动器。

ex.q: Give three advantages of a live transcription app.
ex.a:
1. Easier communication for hearing impaired people.
2. Automatic notes in lessons/meetings.
3. Less typing → less RSI.
ex.az: 方便听障沟通；自动笔记；减少 RSI。

ex.q: How should you set up a tablet for a 70-year-old father?
ex.a:
1. Bigger font (and display zoom).
2. A simple and clean launcher with only key apps.
3. Optionally enable the digital assistant for voice calls.
ex.az: 放大字体；简洁启动器；可开声控。

ex.q: With Voice-over on, how does a user open the Camera app?
ex.a:
1. Tap the Camera icon → phone says "Camera".
2. Double tap anywhere to open it.
ex.az: 单击听到"Camera"，双击开启。

ex.q: "Live transcription apps widen the digital divide because only rich people can use them." Comment.
ex.a:
1. Live transcribe is built into most smartphones for free.
2. It helps the hearing impaired join conversations → it narrows the divide.
ex.az: 多数手机内置免费，帮助听障→缩窄隔阂。

cards.t: Misconception: digital divide only means no Internet
cards.tz: 误解：数码隔阂只是没有网络
cards.en:
Wrong 1: "94% of HK homes have Internet, so there is no digital divide."
Correct: the divide has three aspects: hardware and software (quality, localisation), Internet connection (stability, speed) and ICT skills and literacy. Someone with a phone and Internet who cannot use online banking or spot fake news is still on the wrong side. Gaps exist by age, education, income, work status, location and disability.

Wrong 2: "Going fully digital (e.g. only digital payment for government services) helps everyone."
Correct: it widens the divide for the elderly and low-income. Good measures keep alternatives and add support.
cards.zh:
错误一："94% 住户有网络，所以没有数码隔阂。"
正确：三方面：硬软件（质量、本地化）、网络（稳定、速度）、技能素养。有手机有网络但不会网上银行、不懂辨别假新闻的人仍处劣势。

错误二："全面数码化（政府服务只收电子支付）对人人有利。"
正确：这会扩大长者和低收入人士的隔阂。好措施要保留其他途径并加以支援。

ex.q: Mr Chan, 75, has a smartphone and home broadband but cannot book a clinic appointment online. Is he affected by the digital divide?
ex.a:
1. He has hardware and connection.
2. He lacks ICT skills and literacy.
3. So yes, the skills aspect.
ex.az: 有硬件网络但缺技能→受影响。

ex.q: A family has Internet but only through a slow, unstable 3G plan. Which aspect?
ex.a: Internet connection: stability and data transfer speed.
ex.az: 网络连接：稳定性、速度。

ex.q: Why can an app only in English create a divide even if everyone has phones?
ex.a:
1. Hardware and software aspect includes localisation.
2. Non-English speakers cannot use it fully.
ex.az: 软件本地化不足。

ex.q: A council plans to accept only e-payment at public pools "to help everyone go digital". Evaluate.
ex.a:
1. Elderly and low-income residents without e-wallets are shut out.
2. This widens the divide.
3. Better: keep cash/Octopus, and offer e-payment training.
ex.az: 会排斥长者和低收入者；应保留其他付款方式并提供培训。

cards.en:
Intuition: every "upgrade" leaves an old gadget behind. Where does it go?

Eager to follow trends, we often replace products even when they still work. Disposed products become electronic waste (e-waste). In 2019, 53.6 million tonnes were produced worldwide.
