1. Education licences are often non-commercial.
2. Paid work breaks the terms → may infringe.
3. Check the licence; buy a commercial one if needed.
ex.az: 教育授权多不可商用。

ex.q: Common mistake: "I paid for the app, so I own its copyright and can share it."
ex.a:
1. You bought a licence to use.
2. The developer keeps copyright.
3. Sharing copies breaks the licence.
ex.az: 付费 = 使用权，不能分享副本。

cards.t: Four types of software licence compared
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Four kinds of shops: a normal shop (pay), a free sample stall (try then pay), a free giveaway (take it, can't change it), and an open kitchen (free, and you can see and change the recipe).

The rule:

CommercialSharewareFreewareOpen source
PriceLicence feeFree trial (time/feature-limited); adsFreeFree
UsersSingle/multi/siteLike commercialUnlimitedUnlimited
Source codeNoNoNoYes: use, modify, copy, distribute
Copy / redistributeNoNoYesYes
Commercial useIn feeIn feeMaybe restrictedFree
SupportYesYesLimitedLimited
ExamplesMS Office, PhotoshopWinZip, Lightworks, PhotopeaChrome, Edge, WhatsApp, SignalLinux, Firefox, GIMP, Android

Exam wording: Only open source software gives access to the source code. Shareware is a free trial that is time-limited or feature-limited.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：四种店：普通店（付钱）、试食摊（先试后买）、免费派发（拿走但不能改）、开放厨房（免费，可以看和改食谱）。

规则：

商业共享免费开源
价钱授权费免费试用（限时/限功能）免费免费
源代码无无无有
复制/分发否否可可
技术支持有有少少

考试写法（Exam wording）：Only open source software gives access to the source code.

ex.q: Software P is free and Lily may edit its code; Software Q is free for 30 days. Classify.
ex.a:
1. Q: time-limited trial → shareware.
2. P: free + code editable → open source.
ex.az: Q 共享软件；P 开源。

ex.q: Classify: Firefox, WinZip, Microsoft Office, WhatsApp.
ex.a: Firefox → open source; WinZip → shareware; MS Office → commercial; WhatsApp → freeware.
ex.az: 开源、共享、商业、免费。

ex.q: Common mistake: "Chrome is free, so it's open source."
ex.a:
1. Free ≠ open source.
2. Chrome is freeware: you cannot get and modify its source code.
3. Open source must give source code access.
ex.az: 免费不等于开源。

cards.t: Choosing a licence type as a user
cards.tz: 用户角度：选择软件类型
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Choosing software is like choosing a phone plan: pay more for service and support, or pay less and help yourself.

The rule:

ProsCons
CommercialFrequent updates, technical support, ads-freeHigher cost; cannot modify code
SharewareBasic features free; trial before buying; updates and supportCannot modify code; pay for full/premium; ads
FreewareFree; copy and redistribute freelyCannot modify code; less support; maybe personal use only
Open sourceFree; view/modify code; publish modified version; simpler licence purchaseLess technical support

Exam wording: For shareware: advanced features may be available only when you purchase and it is only free for the trial period.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：选软件像选电话计划：多付钱有服务支援，少付钱就要自己搞定。

规则：

优点缺点
商业常更新、技术支持、无广告贵、不能改代码
共享基本功能免费、可先试完整版要付费、有广告
免费免费、可分发不能改、支持少、或限个人用
开源免费、可看可改技术支持少

考试写法（Exam wording）：Shareware 缺点：advanced features only when you purchase；only free for the trial period。

ex.q: David wants video editing software for vlogs. One pro and con each for commercial and open source.
ex.a:
1. Commercial: pro = updates + support; con = higher cost.
2. Open source: pro = free, can modify; con = less support.
ex.az: 商业：支持好/贵；开源：免费可改/支持少。

ex.q: A small NGO with no IT staff and little money needs an office suite. Suggest a type with a reason.
ex.a:
1. Little money → avoid commercial.
2. Open source (e.g. OpenOffice): free, no licence purchasing.
3. Accept less support, or use community help.
ex.az: 开源：免费，但支持少。

ex.q: Common mistake: "A disadvantage of shareware is that others may modify its source code."
ex.a:
1. Shareware does not release source code.
2. Real cons: pay for advanced features, free only for the trial.
ex.az: 共享软件不公开源代码，此说错。

cards.t: Choosing a licence type as a developer
cards.tz: 开发者角度：选择授权模式
cards.en:
Think of it like this: As a maker you choose: sell tickets (money, fewer users), give free samples with ads, give it away (fame), or open the kitchen to helpers (teamwork).

The rule:

ProsCons
CommercialEarn from each purchase/subscription; users can't copy/redistributeFewer users
SharewareEarn from ads; persuade users to buy during trialNo income if ads blocked or users don't pay
FreewareUsers can't modify code; can redistribute; more usersNo licence income
Open sourceUsers study/modify code; co-develop with users; more usersNo licence income

Exam wording: Shareware lets a developer make money for authorising use, not give up copyright, and attract more people to try it.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：作为开发者你可以：卖票（有钱、用户少）、广告+试用、免费派（多人用）、开放厨房（大家一起改）。

规则：

优点缺点
商业每次购买有收入用户少
共享广告收入、试用期说服购买用户屏蔽广告/不付费就没收入
免费不让人改代码、多人用无授权收入
开源与用户合作开发、多人用无授权收入

考试写法（Exam wording）：Shareware：make money for authorising use, not give up copyright, attract more people to try it。

ex.q: An indie developer wants many users, no code changes by others, and doesn't need income. Which licence?
ex.a:
1. Many users + redistribution → free.
2. No modification → source not released.
3. → Freeware.
ex.az: 免费软件。

ex.q: A university team wants volunteers worldwide to help fix bugs. Which licence?
ex.a:
1. Others must read and modify code.
2. → Open source: cooperate with users to develop.
ex.az: 开源。

ex.q: Common mistake: "Publish as shareware so others can improve the source code together."
ex.a:
1. Improving code together is a reason for open source.
2. Shareware hides the source code.
3. Shareware reasons: income, keep copyright, attract trials.
ex.az: 一起改代码是开源的理由。

cards.t: Misconception: freeware and open source are not uncopyrighted
cards.tz: 误解：免费及开源软件也有版权
cards.en:
Think of it like this: A free gift still has a giver. Free and open source software still belong to their authors; they just let you use them under rules.

The rule:

  • Only public domain software is uncopyrighted.
  • Freeware, shareware, open source and commercial software only grant users rights to use the software under different licence agreements.
  • Breaking open source terms (e.g. removing the licence notice) can still be infringement.
  • If Lily modifies open source Software P, the original author keeps copyright of the original code; Lily owns only her new contributions.
  • Similarity: freeware and open source are both free to use, copy and redistribute. Difference: only open source allows access to and modification of the source code.

Exam wording: Only public domain software is uncopyrighted. Freeware, shareware, open source and commercial software only grant users rights to use the software under different licence agreements.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：免费礼物也有送礼人。免费和开源软件仍属作者，只是按规则让你用。

规则：

  • Only public domain software is uncopyrighted.
  • 四类软件都只是按不同协议授予使用权。
  • 违反开源条款（如删除授权声明）仍可侵权。
  • Lily 改了开源软件 P，原作者仍拥有原代码版权，Lily 只拥有自己新增部分。
  • 相同：都可免费使用、复制、分发。不同：只有开源可取得及修改源代码。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Only public domain software is uncopyrighted.

ex.q: One similarity and one difference between freeware and open source.
ex.a:
1. Similarity: both free to use, copy, redistribute.
2. Difference: only open source gives access to modify source code.
ex.az: 同：免费可分发；异：只有开源可改源码。

ex.q: Lily modifies most of Software P (open source) and redistributes it. Who owns what?
ex.a:
1. Original author keeps copyright of original code.
2. Lily owns her new contributions.
3. She must follow the open source licence.
ex.az: 原作者保留原代码版权；Lily 拥有新部分。

ex.q: Common mistake: "Freeware is free, so I can sell it on my website."
ex.a:
1. Freeware is still copyrighted.
2. Licence allows free use/redistribution, not selling or modifying.
3. Selling it = infringement.
ex.az: 免费软件仍有版权，不能拿来卖。

cards.t: User licence: single-user, multi-user and site licence
cards.tz: 用户授权：单用户、多用户、场地授权
cards.en:
Think of it like this: A single-user licence is a one-person ticket. A multi-user licence is a group ticket. A site licence is a pass for everyone inside one building.

The rule:

  • Commercial/shareware licences state the number of authorised users for each licence.
  • Single-user licence: installed on only one device or only one user can use the software at a time.
  • Multi-user / site licence: unlimited or a defined number of users from a company, organisation or institute.
  • A site licence may limit use to a particular location.
  • Family plan: a defined number of people living together.

Exam wording: A single-user licence allows the software to be installed on only one device or used by only one user at a time.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：单用户授权是一人票；多用户授权是团体票；场地授权是一栋楼里人人可用的通行证。

规则：

  • 授权会注明授权用户数目。
  • Single-user licence：只可装在一部装置或同一时间一人使用。
  • Multi-user / site licence：公司/机构内无限或指定数目用户。
  • Site licence 可能限制在特定地点使用。
  • 家庭计划：同住的指定人数。

考试写法（Exam wording）：single-user: only one device / one user at a time；site licence: may limit use at a particular location。

ex.q: A school with 40 PCs buys one single-user licence and activates it on all PCs. Problem and fix?
ex.a:
1. Allows only 1 device → 39 unauthorised copies.
2. = copyright infringement.
3. Fix: buy a site licence or a multi-user licence for 40.
ex.az: 39 份未授权；改买场地/多用户授权。

ex.q: A company has 10 staff who all need the software at the same time. How many single-user licences?
ex.a:
1. Single-user = one user at a time.
2. 10 people at once → 10 licences (or one 10-user multi-user licence).
ex.az: 10 份或一个 10 人授权。

ex.q: Common mistake: "With a site licence, staff can install it at home too."
ex.a:
1. A site licence may limit use to a particular location.
2. Home is outside the site.
3. Read the agreement before installing elsewhere.
ex.az: 场地授权可能只限该地点。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Instead of buying a car, you pay monthly for a ride app. SaaS is renting software that lives on the company's computers in the cloud.

The rule:

  • Old: one-off licence fee. New: subscription model that treats software as a service, paid monthly or annually.
  • SaaS is also known as web-based software because it is centrally hosted by the software company based on cloud computing.
  • Provider hosts servers, database, code, application, help desk; business, institutional and personal users connect over the Internet.
  • Examples: Microsoft 365, Adobe Creative Cloud, Zoom, Teams, Spotify, Netflix.

Exam wording: SaaS is also known as web-based software because it is centrally hosted by the software company based on cloud computing; users pay for the licence monthly or annually.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：不买车，按月付钱用叫车 app。SaaS 就是“租用”放在公司云端电脑上的软件。

规则：

  • 旧：one-off licence fee；新：subscription，每月或每年付费。
  • SaaS is also known as web-based software because it is centrally hosted … based on cloud computing.
  • 供应商在云端管理服务器、数据库、代码、应用、支援；用户经互联网使用。
  • 例：Microsoft 365、Adobe CC、Zoom、Spotify、Netflix。

考试写法（Exam wording）：SaaS … centrally hosted by the software company based on cloud computing。

ex.q: Why is SaaS also called web-based software?
ex.a:
1. Software is centrally hosted by the company on cloud servers.
2. Users access it through the Internet.
3. Not installed and run fully locally.
ex.az: 集中托管于云端，经互联网使用。

ex.q: A school moves from installed Office 2016 to Microsoft 365. Name two changes for IT staff.
ex.a:
1. No need to manage installation/servers; updates applied centrally.
2. Must pay yearly and need Internet.
ex.az: 不用管安装更新；要年费和网络。

ex.q: Common mistake: "After I cancel my Spotify subscription, I still own the songs I saved."
ex.a:
1. SaaS = paying for access, not ownership.
2. When the subscription ends, access stops.
ex.az: 订阅结束即失去使用权。

frames.en: The company hosts servers, database, code and help desk in the cloud.
frames.zh: 供应商在云端托管一切。

frames.en: User pays monthly/annually and logs in with an account.
frames.zh: 用户按月/年付费并登入。

frames.en: Requests and data travel over the Internet; the app runs on the provider's servers.
frames.zh: 经互联网使用，程序在供应商服务器运行。

frames.en: Updates are installed centrally, so every user gets them at once.
frames.zh: 集中更新，全部用户同时获得。

cards.tz: 永久授权 vs 订阅
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Buying a book (pay once, keep forever, works offline) vs a library membership (pay monthly, always the newest books, but you need to go there).

The rule:

Perpetual licenceSubscription
ProsIndefinite use with one-off payment; no Internet needed; faster response; better security control (no data on cloud)Trial period; cloud backup; simpler installation; multiple devices by login; free frequent updates and support
ConsExtra costs for maintenance/updates; limited to a certain number of devicesInternet may be required; longer response time
ExamplesOffice Home and Student 2019; Adobe CS6Netflix, Spotify, Zoom, Adobe CC, Microsoft 365

Exam wording: Perpetual: indefinite use with one-off payment, Internet connection not required. Subscription: access on multiple devices by account login, free frequent updates.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：买书（付一次、永远拥有、离线可读）vs 图书馆会员（按月付、总有新书，但要去馆）。

规则：

永久授权订阅
优点一次付款永久使用；不需上网；反应快；保安较好有试用期；云端备份；安装简单；多装置登入；免费更新与支援
缺点维护/更新另收费；限装置数目或需上网；反应较慢

考试写法（Exam wording）：永久：one-off payment, Internet not required；订阅：multiple devices by login, free frequent updates。

ex.q: A law firm with confidential files and unreliable Internet: perpetual or subscription? Two reasons.
ex.a:
1. Perpetual.
2. Works without Internet.
3. Better security control: no data sent to cloud.
ex.az: 永久授权：不需网络、保安较好。

ex.q: A freelancer works on a desktop, laptop and tablet and wants the newest features. Which?
ex.a:
1. Subscription.
2. Multiple devices by account login.
3. Free frequent updates + cloud backup.
ex.az: 订阅。

ex.q: Common mistake: "A perpetual licence means I get all future versions free forever."
ex.a:
1. Perpetual = use this version forever.
2. Additional costs may be charged for updates/maintenance.
ex.az: 永久授权不包括所有新版本。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Anyone can copy a lock-box, but it won't open without the key. The installer is the box; the licence key is the key only paying customers get.

The rule:

  • Licence key (activation key, product key): a string of characters given to an authorised user who has paid for the software.
  • During installation, the user enters the licence key to register or activate the software.
  • Copied installer alone is useless; vendor can limit activations per key.
  • Hardware key (USB dongle): a physical device plugged into USB for unlocking the software; also used for two-factor authentication.
  • Licence keys support device-locked and user-locked licences.

Exam wording: A licence key is a string of characters given to an authorised user who has paid for the software; it is entered during installation to register or activate the software.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：谁都能复制一个锁箱，但没钥匙打不开。安装档是箱，序号就是只有付费用户才有的钥匙。

规则：

  • Licence key：a string of characters given to an authorised user who has paid。
  • 安装时输入序号以注册或启动软件。
  • 只复制安装档没用；厂商可限制每个序号的启动次数。
  • Hardware key（USB dongle）：插入 USB 以解锁软件，也可作双重认证。

考试写法（Exam wording）：a string of characters given to an authorised user who has paid … entered to register or activate the software。

ex.q: Why does a licence key reduce piracy compared with only selling a downloadable installer?
ex.a:
1. Installer can be copied freely.
2. Software won't run without a valid key given only to payers.
3. Vendor limits activations, so sharing one key fails.
ex.az: 无序号不能运行，且限启动次数。

ex.q: A CAD program only runs when a USB dongle is plugged in. What is this and why use it?
ex.a:
1. Hardware key.
2. Physical, so hard to copy like a text key.
3. Unlocks the software only for the holder.
ex.az: 硬件钥匙，难复制。

ex.q: Common mistake: "I'll post my key online so my friends can activate too; it's my key."
ex.a:
1. The key is given to one authorised paying user.
2. Sharing it = unauthorised use; activations will also be blocked.
ex.az: 序号只授权给付费用户，分享即违规。

frames.en: User pays and receives a licence key (e.g. ABCDE-12345-…).
frames.zh: 付款取得序号。

frames.en: User installs the software; it asks for the key.
frames.zh: 安装时要求输入序号。

frames.en: Software sends the key to the vendor; vendor checks it is valid and counts activations.
frames.zh: 软件把序号送往厂商检查。

frames.en: Valid → activated. Too many activations or fake key → 'Invalid licence key'.
frames.zh: 有效则启动，否则显示 Invalid licence key。

cards.tz: 锁定装置 vs 锁定用户授权
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Device-locked = the key is glued to one computer. User-locked = the key follows you (your account) to any computer you sign in on.

The rule:

Device-lockedUser-locked
Locked toMachine ID (unique code of a device)User account
DevicesSingle device (some allow a few)Any device while signed in
UsersOne at a timeUsually one at a time
ActivationKey + machine ID at installationRegistration; agree to terms
  • Too many activations → 'Invalid licence key'.
  • User-locked is an example of a floating licence (install on multiple devices).

Exam wording: Device-locked: the licence key is locked to the unique machine ID of your device. User-locked: the licence key is locked to a specific account; users can use it on any device but must remain signed in.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：锁定装置 = 序号黏在一部电脑上；锁定用户 = 序号跟着你的帐户走，任何电脑登入即可。

规则：

锁定装置锁定用户
锁定于Machine ID用户帐户
装置单一（或少数）任何（须登入）
启动安装时绑定机器码注册、同意条款
  • 超出次数 → 'Invalid licence key'。
  • User-locked 是 floating licence 的一种。

考试写法（Exam wording）：locked to the unique machine ID vs locked to a specific account … remain signed in。

ex.q: Kelly reinstalls a device-locked program on her new laptop with the same key and gets 'Invalid licence key'. Why?
ex.a:
1. Key was locked to the old machine ID.
2. Maximum activations reached.
3. Deactivate old device or contact vendor.
ex.az: 序号绑定旧机器码且已达上限。

ex.q: Adobe CC lets Joe use the app on home and school PCs after signing in. Which type?
ex.a:
1. Locked to his account, any device, must stay signed in.
2. → User-locked (floating licence).
ex.az: 锁定用户。

ex.q: Common mistake: "User-locked means my whole family can use it at the same time on different devices."
ex.a:
1. It is locked to one account.
2. Single-user licence: usually one user at a time.
3. Family needs a family/multi-user plan.
ex.az: 通常同一时间一人；家人要买家庭计划。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: A visible watermark is a big stamp across a photo. An invisible one is like secret ink: you can't see it, but a special tool can read it, even after the photo is cut or shrunk.

The rule:

  • Digital watermark technology is embedding data into a digital work (images, videos, text…).
  • Visible: a mark made clear to the user.
  • Invisible: embedded but cannot be seen, and extracted using watermarking algorithms.
  • Invisible is popular: harder to remove, does not affect the carrying object, remains and can be extracted after cropping, resizing and compression.
  • Insertion: original + watermark bits → watermarked data. Extraction: modified copy → watermark still found.

Exam wording: Invisible watermarks are harder to remove, do not affect the carrying object, and can still be extracted even after cropping, resizing and compression.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：可见水印是盖在相片上的大印章；隐形水印像隐形墨水：看不到，但特别工具可读出，即使相片被裁剪或缩小。

规则：

  • Digital watermark: embedding data into a digital work。
  • Visible：用户看得见。
  • Invisible：看不见，用 watermarking algorithms 提取。
  • 隐形水印较受欢迎：难移除、不影响作品、裁剪/缩放/压缩后仍可提取。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Invisible watermarks are harder to remove, do not affect the carrying object, and can be extracted after cropping, resizing and compression.

ex.q: A photographer sells photos online. Two reasons to use an invisible rather than a visible watermark.
ex.a:
1. Does not affect the photo for paying customers.
2. Harder to remove, survives cropping/compression, so ownership can be proved.
ex.az: 不影响相片；难移除。

ex.q: A pirate crops and compresses a watermarked image. Can the owner still prove ownership?
ex.a:
1. Run the watermarking algorithm on the pirated copy.
2. Invisible watermark remains unchanged.
3. Yes, it is extracted as proof.
ex.az: 仍可提取水印证明。

ex.q: Common mistake: "I removed the visible watermark, so the photo is now free to use."
ex.a:
1. Removing a watermark doesn't remove copyright.
2. Uploading it is still infringement.
ex.az: 移除水印不等于没有版权。

frames.en: Original image + watermark bits (0101 1100 0110) → algorithm hides bits in the pixels.
frames.zh: 原图 + 水印位元 → 算法嵌入。

frames.en: The watermarked image looks the same to the eye.
frames.zh: 肉眼看不出分别。

frames.en: Pirate crops, resizes and compresses the image.
frames.zh: 盗版者裁剪、缩放、压缩。

frames.en: Algorithm extracts 0101 1100 0110 from the modified copy → proves ownership.
frames.zh: 算法从修改后副本提取水印 → 证明拥有权。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Give each friend a copy of a secret with a different hidden mark. If it leaks, the mark tells you whose copy it was.

The rule:

ApplicationMethod
Digital copyright protectionOwnership rights are embedded to prove copyright infringement.
Source tracingData given to different recipients is watermarked differently, to trace the person who leaks confidential information.
  • Alibaba (2016) traced the employee who leaked a screenshot of internal news using digital watermarks.
  • To stop unauthorised distribution of images → digital watermark (not digital signature, not SSL).

Exam wording: Data given to different recipients is watermarked differently. This is useful to trace the person who leaks the confidential information.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：给每个朋友一份秘密，各藏不同记号。泄露时，记号就告诉你是谁那份。

规则：

应用方法
Digital copyright protection嵌入拥有权以证明侵权
Source tracing给不同收件人不同水印，追查泄密者
  • 阿里巴巴 2016 年以水印追查泄露截图的员工。
  • 防止图片被未授权分发 → 数码水印（不是数码签署、SSL）。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Data given to different recipients is watermarked differently … to trace the person who leaks the confidential information.

ex.q: A company sends a confidential PDF to 5 partners and a copy leaks. How to find the leaker?
ex.a:
1. Before sending, embed a different invisible watermark (partner ID) in each copy.
2. Extract it from the leaked copy.
3. The ID shows whose copy leaked.
ex.az: 每份嵌入不同 ID，提取即知。

ex.q: A streaming site wants to stop its videos being re-uploaded elsewhere. Which technology helps?
ex.a:
1. Embed ownership with digital watermarks.
2. Pirated uploads can be detected and proven.
ex.az: 数码水印。

ex.q: Common mistake: "Use a digital signature to prevent unauthorised distribution of images."
ex.a:
1. Digital signature verifies the sender and detects modification.
2. SSL encrypts data in transit.
3. Stopping image redistribution → digital watermark.
ex.az: 应选数码水印。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Like a wax seal on a royal letter: you know who sent it, and if anyone opened and changed it, the seal is broken.

The rule:

  • Digital signature is a technology used for verifying the sender's identity.
  • Commonly applied in detecting unauthorised modification and forgery (贗品) such as pirated software.
  • The company signs its program files. If a pirate cracks or adds malware, the signature no longer matches.
  • Check on Windows: right-click → Properties → Digital Signatures tab → signer name, digest algorithm, timestamp.
  • Watermark = ownership/trace source; signature = who sent it and not modified.

Exam wording: Digital signature is used for verifying the sender's identity and detecting unauthorised modification and forgery such as pirated software.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：像皇室信件上的火漆印：知道是谁寄的；若有人拆开改动，印就破了。

规则：

  • Digital signature … verifying the sender's identity.
  • 用于侦测未经授权的修改和伪造（如盗版软件）。
  • 公司为程序签署；盗版者破解或加入恶意程序后，签署不再吻合。
  • Windows：右键 → Properties → Digital Signatures → 签署人、摘要算法、时间。

考试写法（Exam wording）：verifying the sender's identity … detecting unauthorised modification and forgery such as pirated software。

ex.q: You download an installer claiming to be from Adobe. How do you check it is genuine?
ex.a:
1. Right-click → Properties → Digital Signatures.
2. Signer should be the real company (e.g. Adobe Systems) and valid.
3. Missing/invalid → modified or forged.
ex.az: 查看数码签署。

ex.q: A cracked game was edited to skip licence checks. Why does Windows warn the signature is invalid?
ex.a:
1. Original files were signed by the developer.
2. Any change makes the file no longer match the signature.
3. So modification is detected.
ex.az: 修改后签署不吻合。

ex.q: Common mistake: "A digital signature stops people from copying the program."
ex.a:
1. It does not stop copying.
2. It verifies sender and detects modification.
3. To prove ownership/trace copies → watermark; to stop use → licence key.
ex.az: 签署不能阻止复制，只验证来源和完整性。

demo.title: How a digital signature detects tampering

frames.en: Developer signs the program file with its private key.
frames.zh: 开发商用私钥签署程序。

frames.en: User downloads the file with its signature.
frames.zh: 用户下载档案及签署。

frames.en: User's computer checks the signature with the developer's public key.
frames.zh: 电脑用公钥检查。

frames.en: Match → genuine, unmodified. Mismatch → modified or forged (e.g. pirated).
frames.zh: 吻合 → 正版；不吻合 → 被改/伪造。

cards.tz: 必须上网的应用：以加密防盗版
cards.en:
Think of it like this: The game keeps its most important parts (your coins, HP) locked in the company's safe. Each time you play, the safe sends you a locked box only the real app can open.

The rule:

  1. User opens the game; it connects to the Internet.
  2. The server performs data encryption on important data/commands, e.g. in-game currency, HP, MP.
  3. Server sends encrypted data to the device.
  4. The device performs data decryption and runs the game.
  • Aim: prevent illegal modification of the app such as cheating and pirated games.
  • Cost: no offline mode; uses mobile data.

Exam wording: When the game connects to the Internet, it is processing data encryption and decryption, which aims to prevent illegal modification of the app such as cheating and pirated games.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：游戏把最重要的部分（金币、HP）锁在公司的保险箱。每次玩，保险箱寄来一个只有正版 app 打得开的锁盒。

规则：

  1. 用户开游戏，连上网。
  2. 服务器把重要数据（游戏币、HP、MP）加密。
  3. 传送加密数据到装置。
  4. 装置解密后运行游戏。
  • 目的：prevent illegal modification of the app such as cheating and pirated games。
  • 代价：不能离线、耗流量。

考试写法（Exam wording）：… processing data encryption and decryption … to prevent illegal modification of the app such as cheating and pirated games.

ex.q: A single-player game shows 'No Connection – Try Again' offline. How does this protect the developer's IP?
ex.a:
1. Key data are encrypted on the server.
2. Only decrypted on the device after connecting.
3. Pirated/modified copies can't get valid data → stops piracy and cheating.
ex.az: 服务器加密关键数据，盗版无法取得。

ex.q: A player edits the local save file to give himself 999,999 coins. Why doesn't it work in an online-only game?
ex.a:
1. Coin values come from the server, encrypted.
2. The local edit is ignored/overwritten.
3. Cheating by modifying the app fails.
ex.az: 币值来自服务器，改本地无效。

ex.q: Common mistake: "It needs Internet only because of online multiplayer."
ex.a:
1. Even single-player games may need it.
2. The connection is for encryption/decryption of key data.
3. Purpose: anti-piracy and anti-cheating.
ex.az: 联网是为加密解密以防盗版作弊。

frames.en: The game app connects to the developer's server.
frames.zh: 游戏连接服务器。

frames.en: Server encrypts coins, HP, MP and commands.
frames.zh: 服务器加密数据。

frames.en: Encrypted data travel to the device.
frames.zh: 传送加密数据。

frames.en: The genuine app decrypts and runs. A cracked offline copy gets nothing.
frames.zh: 正版 app 解密运行；破解版无法取得。

mc.q: Which of the following actions may be seen as copyright infringement?
o: Downloading articles from an academic database.
Broadcasting a school event with permission.
Uploading films to the cloud storage and sharing them with friends.
Sending selfies to friends using peer-to-peer (P2P) software.
mc.e: Sharing copyrighted films without permission is unauthorised distribution (Internet piracy).
mc.ez: 未经许可分享电影属互联网盗版。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC1 (p.108)

mc.q: Janice takes the following actions on her work computer. Which of them is considered legal?
o: Sharing a commercial software with friends via the cloud.
Buying a CD and using the music in an event promotional video.
Using peer-to-peer (P2P) software to download a movie for personal use.
Sending freeware to colleagues via a BT program.
mc.e: Freeware may be copied and redistributed freely.
mc.ez: 免费软件可自由复制及分发。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC2 (p.108)

mc.q: Which may be considered copyright infringement? (1) Screenshot of a free online newspaper posted on social media (2) Using photos from an official website to sell a used product online (3) Photocopying one page of a 36-page recipe book for a school assignment (4) Removing the watermark from a copyrighted photo and uploading it to a personal website
mc.e: (3) is limited use for education (fair dealing); the others use works without permission.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC3 (p.108)

mc.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes copyright in Hong Kong?
o: Copyright only protects high quality works.
Copyright owners cannot transfer their copyrights to others.
Copyright owners are required to put a copyright symbol '©' on their work for a higher level of copyright protection.
mc.e: Copyright is given automatically when a work is completed; no registration or notice is needed.
mc.ez: 版权自动产生，毋须注册或声明。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC4 (p.108)

mc.q: Which of the following statements about freeware is correct?
o: The software is allowed to be installed on a single device only.
The source code is free to modify.
The software is free to make copies.
Distribution of the software is not allowed.
mc.e: Freeware: unlimited users, copying and redistribution allowed, no source code access.
mc.ez: 免费软件可复制，但不能改源码。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC5 (p.108)

mc.q: Ms Lee downloads an open source image editor. What can she do? (1) Edit posters for commercial purposes (2) Add her own code to the program (3) Send the modified version to her friends
mc.e: Open source is free for commercial use and may be modified and redistributed.
mc.ez: 开源可商用、修改及分发。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC6 (p.108)

mc.q: Which is/are the major characteristic(s) of freeware? (1) Free to use for non-commercial purposes (2) The developer can modify the source code (3) Users can access the source code (4) Users need permission from the copyright owner before using it
mc.e: Freeware is free to use (at least non-commercially); users cannot access the source code and need no extra permission.
mc.ez: 免费软件可免费使用，用户看不到源码。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC7 (p.108)

mc.q: Which can help prevent unauthorised distribution of digital images? (1) Digital watermark (2) Digital signature (3) Secure Socket Layer (SSL)
mc.e: Watermarks embed ownership/trace sources; signatures verify senders; SSL only encrypts transmission.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC8 (p.109)

mc.q: Peter writes a program on his own. Which are his rights as copyright owner? (1) Translate and publish it in another language (2) Charge a licence fee for the right to use it (3) Sell the copyright to another company (4) Transfer ownership of the software to others
mc.e: All are exclusive rights: adapt/translate, grant use for royalties, sell, transfer.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC9 (p.109)

mc.q: Reasons for developers to publish software as shareware? (1) Make money for authorising others to use it (2) Do not want to give up copyright (3) Want more people to improve the source code together (4) Want to attract more people to try it
mc.e: Improving source code together is a reason for open source, not shareware.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC10 (p.109)

mc.q: Which is/are the exception(s) to copyright infringement? (1) Scanning workbooks and distributing copies to students (2) Printing and distributing sheet music written in 1866 (3) Activating software on all school computers with a single-device licence key (4) Showing TV broadcasts in restaurants with permission from the copyright owner
mc.e: 1866 music's copyright has expired; (4) has permission. (1) and (3) are unauthorised copying.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC11 (p.109)

mc.q: Which use of copyrighted work is considered legal in Hong Kong?
o: Buying an activation key with a cheaper price from a software pirate.
Selling pirated products in the Lunar New Year Fair.
Photocopying one page from a reference book that cannot be borrowed for a school project.
Sharing copies of lecture notes made by your school teacher with friends in other schools.
mc.e: Copying one page for a school project is limited, fair educational use.
mc.ez: 影印一页作功课属公平处理。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC12 (p.109)

mc.q: What is the legal consequence of selling copies of your own HKDSE past papers on social media?
o: The Innovation and Technology Commission (ITC) will take legal action.
Your action is considered a civil offence.
HKEAA can report the case to the Customs and Excise Department for further investigation.
No legal consequence because copyright does not protect digital files on the Internet.
mc.e: HKEAA owns copyright of submitted work; selling pirated copies is a criminal matter handled by C&ED.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC13 (p.109)

mc.q: Cindy uploads photos without the watermark '© All rights reserved'. Which statement is correct?
o: The social media company will own the copyright.
Cindy has to register for copyright protection.
Cindy owns the copyright without declaration.
mc.e: Copyright is automatic; ideas are not protected, only their tangible expression.
mc.ez: 版权自动拥有，毋须声明。

mc.q: What is the legal consequence of sharing a commercial Chinese input software with friends via a cloud drive?
o: You may be sued for copyright infringement through a civil lawsuit.
You may be liable to imprisonment.
Your action may be considered a criminal offence.
You will need to pay fines to the Customs and Excise Department.
mc.e: The copyright owner can seek monetary compensation through a civil lawsuit.
mc.ez: 版权持有人可提出民事诉讼。

mc.q: Patrick bought cracked software at half the legal price. What is NOT a possible consequence?
o: His computer may be attacked because bug-fix updates cannot be installed.
The copyright owner will offer a customised free trial for Patrick.
The act violates intellectual property rights.
mc.e: Pirates get no support or offers from the owner.
mc.ez: 版权持有人不会给盗版用户试用。

mc.q: Peter posts photos of old housing estates online. Which actions are illegal? (1) A publisher uses the photos in a textbook (2) A teacher shows one photo in a lesson (3) A friend reposts them on social media (4) A friend prints a photo with his permission
mc.e: Only fair non-profit educational use is exempt; (4) has permission.
mc.ez: 只有非牟利教学豁免，(4)有许可。

mc.q: Which use is most likely to be fair dealing?
o: Copy an entire article from a website into a school assignment.
Show an entire film during an English lesson.
Play a few minutes of a documentary to illustrate a historical event.
Distribute copies of HKDSE past papers to students without paying any fee.

mc.q: Which is NOT considered copyright infringement in Hong Kong?
o: Using copyrighted music for an advertisement competition without paying any fee.
Sharing your single-user streaming subscription account with friends.
Uploading a travel vlog taken by you on a video sharing website.
Broadcasting gameplay on a live streaming platform.
mc.e: You own the copyright of your own vlog.
mc.ez: 自己拍的 vlog 版权属自己。

mc.q: HKEAA owns the copyright of all work submitted by candidates. Which is least likely to be infringement?
o: You sell copies of your submitted answer scripts.
You photocopy your submitted answer scripts and give them to friends.
You write examination strategies according to your submitted answers.
You share your SBA video submitted to HKEAA on social media.
mc.e: Writing your own strategies uses ideas, not copies of the work.
mc.ez: 写自己的策略不涉复制作品。

mc.q: A tutor photocopies a whole book and distributes copies to students. What can the copyright holders do?
o: Complain to the Customs and Excise Department about the pirated copies.
Complain to the Intellectual Property Department about the pirated copies.
Nothing, because it is for educational purposes.
mc.e: C&ED takes criminal sanctions; copying a whole book is not fair dealing.

mc.q: George wants to use shareware X to edit vlogs. Disadvantage(s)? (1) Source code will be modified by others (2) Advanced features may be available only when you purchase (3) It is only free for the trial period (4) Technical support may not be provided
mc.e: Shareware has trial/feature limits; it usually does provide support.
mc.ez: 共享软件限时限功能，但有支援。

mc.q: Patrick installed video editing software free for educational use and now has a freelance job. What should he do first?
o: Read the licence agreement to check if it can be used for commercial purposes.
mc.e: Educational licences may forbid commercial use.
mc.ez: 先看授权是否容许商用。

mc.q: Which can protect IP from unauthorised use of videos posted on online streaming sites? (1) Digital signature (2) Avoid opening links from unknown users (3) Digital watermarks
mc.e: Watermarks prove ownership/trace copies; signatures verify the sender only.

mc.q: What is the legal consequence of selling cracked apps on online shopping platforms?
o: The Intellectual Property Department will take criminal sanctions.
You will not be arrested unless the copyright holder complains.
Your action may be considered a criminal offence.
The OGCIO processes copyright infringement complaints.
mc.e: Only C&ED takes criminal sanctions, even without a complaint.
mc.ez: 可构成刑事罪行，海关可主动执法。

mc.q: Intellectual property is best described as
o: physical goods produced by a company
a set of separate intangible asset rights over creations of the intellect
the hardware and software owned by a person
any information found on the Internet
mc.e: IP = creation of intellect; intangible asset rights.
mc.ez: 知识产权是一组无形财产权。

mc.q: Which type of intellectual property does NOT require registration in Hong Kong?
mc.e: Except for copyright, other IP types all require registration.

mc.q: The unique shape and curved edges of a new smartphone body are best protected by
mc.e: Registered design protects new and distinctive appearance.

mc.q: A mobile app's icon and name are best protected by
mc.e: Trademark: unique sign distinguishing products; examples include app name and icon.

mc.q: Which statement about patents is correct?
o: Computer programs can never be patented.
A computer program can be patented if it solves a technical problem.
Patents protect the appearance of a product.
mc.e: Book: computer programs can be patented if they solve a technical problem.
mc.ez: 解决技术问题的程序可获专利。

mc.q: What does the symbol ® indicate?
o: The work is in the public domain

mc.q: A court held that selfies taken by a monkey are in the public domain because
o: the camera owner did not register them
only works created by humans are protected by copyright

mc.q: In general, copyright in Hong Kong lasts until
o: 50 years after the death of the creator

mc.q: Which is protected as a 'typographical arrangement of a published edition'?
o: The interface layout of a published website

mc.q: Which of the following is NOT protected by copyright?
o: The idea of making a photo-sharing app
mc.e: Ideas are not protected; only their tangible expression.

mc.q: Which is NOT an exclusive right of a copyright owner?
o: Passing the copyright to others in a will
Stopping others from criticising the work in a review
mc.e: Criticism and review is fair dealing.

Showing it in class with credit

o: Streaming a song on a licensed music app
Buying a cracked membership of software on an online shopping site
Downloading Firefox from its official site

mc.q: Which is a security risk of using pirated software?
mc.e: Pirated software may carry malware and cause data breaches.

o: Watching a licensed film on Netflix
Live streaming copyrighted songs without permission
Quoting a sentence in a review

mc.q: Non-commercial distribution of pirated copies is
o: a crime if it harms the interest of the copyright owners
mc.ez: 损害版权人利益即属犯罪。

mc.q: Fair dealing allows
o: limited use of a copyrighted work without permission for certain purposes

mc.q: Which is NOT a fair dealing purpose listed in the book?

o: Showing parts of a TV programme for instruction

Downloading and distributing a whole e-textbook to students
Printing part of a journal article for personal study

mc.q: Which statement about plagiarism is correct?
o: Plagiarism is using another person's work without acknowledgement.
Plagiarism is a criminal offence handled by Customs.
Citing the source turns piracy into fair dealing.
mc.e: Plagiarism is unethical; infringement is illegal; not always overlapping.

mc.q: Using copyrighted images in class presentation slides without credit is most likely

o: The site may obtain the right to reuse uploaded content

sq.q: Lily plans to use a program to manage the inventory of her online store. Software P is free and allows her to edit the code; Software Q is only free for 30 days.

parts.q: Which software is published under a shareware licence?
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Software Q (free only for a time-limited trial).

parts.q: Lily modifies most of the source code of software P and redistributes it. Who owns the copyright of the redistributed version?
parts.ms: Suggested answer: The original author/developer still owns the copyright of the original code (open source software is still copyrighted); Lily only owns her own modifications and must follow the open source licence.

sq.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise LQ1 (p.110)

sq.q: Janice uses page-layout software to make a photo book for her friend's birthday.

parts.q: Program X is commercial design software. A blogger has uploaded a trial version to his cloud storage. State TWO reasons why Janice should not download it from there.
parts.ms:
Any two:
It may be modified and contain malware/virus (data breach).
It is not authorised by the copyright owner, so downloading may be copyright infringement.
No official updates/technical support.

parts.q: Janice downloads the trial from the official website. What should she read to learn about the rights granted?
parts.ms: The licence agreement / terms and conditions (end-user licence agreement).

parts.q: She finds pictures under CC BY-ND. What should she do to avoid copyright infringement?
parts.ms: Give credit to the contributor (title, creator, licence) and use the pictures without modification (no derivatives).

sq.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise LQ2 (p.110)

sq.q: David plans to install video editing software to edit his vlogs. Compare the types below by stating one advantage and one disadvantage of each.

parts.q: Commercial software
parts.ms:
Pro: frequent updates and technical support / usually ads-free.
Con: higher cost / cannot modify the code.

parts.q: Open source software
parts.ms:
Pro: free to use / can view and modify the source code.
Con: less (limited or no) technical support.

sq.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise LQ3 (p.110)

sq.q: Amy joins the Olympic Games and wins the gold medal.

parts.q: She posts a video of her semifinal performance (filmed by the official broadcaster) on her social media. What is the possible legal consequence?
parts.ms: The broadcaster/copyright owner may sue her for copyright infringement in a civil lawsuit (monetary compensation).

parts.q: Amy posts a vlog about her life in the Olympic village without a © notice. Can news media repost her entire vlog without her permission? Why?
parts.ms:
No.
Copyright is given automatically to the creator; no notice/registration is needed.
Reposting the entire vlog is not limited fair dealing for news reporting, so permission is needed.

sq.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise LQ4 (p.111)

sq.q: A university department purchases a single-user licence for a commercial software program.

parts.q: The department installs it on all office computers. How does this violate the Copyright Ordinance?
parts.ms: A single-user licence allows installation on only one device / one user at a time; the other installations are unauthorised copies.

parts.q: What should the department do to avoid copyright infringement?
parts.ms: Buy a multi-user/site licence (or enough single-user licences for each computer).

sq.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise LQ5 (p.111)

sq.q: Orange Ltd launches a new smartphone with a new folding-display technology, a fruit logo, a distinctive rounded body and its own operating system.

parts.q: Name the type of IP that protects each of: display technology, logo, body appearance, OS source code.
parts.ms:
Display technology: patent
Logo: trademark
Appearance: registered design
Source code: copyright

parts.q: Which of these needs no registration? Explain.
parts.ms:
Copyright (source code).
It is given automatically when the work is created; all other types require registration.

parts.q: Distinguish the symbols ™ and ®.
parts.ms:
™ claims a sign as a trademark (may be unregistered).
® may only be used for a registered trademark.

sq.q: Tom Ho runs an online shop selling 'lifetime activation keys' for a popular office suite at 10% of the official price.

parts.q: Is this a criminal offence or only a civil matter? Explain.
parts.ms:
Criminal offence.
Distributing/selling pirated software for commercial purposes is a criminal offence under the Copyright Ordinance.

parts.q: State the maximum penalty if he sold 2 keys.
parts.ms:
Fine $50,000 per pirated copy = $100,000;
and imprisonment for 4 years.

parts.q: Which department would take criminal action, and can it act if the software company does not complain?
parts.ms:
Customs and Excise Department.
Yes, C&ED can take action even without a complaint from the copyright owner.

parts.q: Give one social and one economic impact of such piracy.
parts.ms:
Social: creators lose income/motivation; pirates' reputation damaged; country's reputation declines.
Economic: lower sales, fewer investors, closures and unemployment, falling tax revenue.

sq.q: ABC Secondary School teachers plan the following: (1) show a 5-minute clip of a documentary in a History lesson; (2) scan a whole workbook and upload it to the school intranet for all students; (3) students attach copyrighted images to a project with credit.

parts.q: Explain the meaning of fair dealing.
parts.ms:
Exceptions in the Copyright Ordinance allowing limited use of copyrighted work
without the owner's permission for purposes such as education, research/private study, criticism/review/news.

parts.q: For each of (1)-(3), state whether it is likely fair dealing, with a reason.
parts.ms:
(1) Fair: only part used for instruction.
(2) Not fair: whole work copied/distributed, replaces purchase.
(3) Fair: limited use in assignment, and crediting avoids plagiarism.

parts.q: If students in (3) did not credit the images, what problem arises, and is it illegal?
parts.ms:
Plagiarism (using others' work without acknowledgement).
It is unethical but not necessarily copyright infringement / illegal.

sq.q: A photo agency sells high-resolution images online and sends confidential product photos to 3 magazines before launch.

parts.q: Distinguish visible and invisible digital watermarks.
parts.ms:
Visible: mark inside the object, clear to the user.
Invisible: embedded, cannot be seen, extracted with watermarking algorithms.

parts.q: Give TWO reasons the agency may prefer invisible watermarks.
parts.ms: Harder to remove; does not affect image quality; remains extractable after cropping/resizing/compression.

parts.q: One confidential photo leaks. Explain how watermarking can find the source.
parts.ms:
Each magazine's copy is watermarked differently (source tracing).
Extract the watermark from the leaked copy to identify which magazine leaked it.

parts.q: Would a digital signature help prevent the leak? Explain.
parts.ms:
No.
A digital signature verifies the sender's identity and detects modification; it does not stop or trace redistribution.

sq.q: A design company compares Adobe Creative Suite 6 (perpetual licence) with Adobe Creative Cloud (subscription, SaaS).

parts.q: What is SaaS?
parts.ms:
Software sold on a subscription (monthly/annually) as a service
centrally hosted by the software company on cloud computing, accessed over the Internet.

parts.q: Give TWO advantages of the subscription for the company.
parts.ms: Any two: trial period; cloud backup; simpler installation; access on multiple devices by login; free frequent updates and ongoing support.

parts.q: Give TWO advantages of the perpetual licence.
parts.ms: Any two: indefinite use with one-off payment; no Internet required; faster response; better security without cloud data transmission.

parts.q: Distinguish a device-locked and a user-locked licence.
parts.ms:
Device-locked: key locked to the machine ID; one device.
User-locked: key locked to an account; any device while signed in.

pr.task: Write attribution(title, creator, licence) that returns the TCL attribution string, e.g. attribution('Cat','Y.Hino','CC BY 2.0') returns "Cat" by Y.Hino is licensed under CC BY 2.0.
pr.taskz: 编写 attribution(title, creator, licence)，按“标题-作者-授权”格式返回署名句子。

tests.expect: '"Cat" by Y.Hino is licensed under CC BY 2.0.'
'"20160314-ZD4_6150" by zhao hui is licensed under CC BY-SA 2.0.'

pr.solution:
def attribution(title, creator, licence):
    return '"' + title + '" by ' + creator + ' is licensed under ' + licence + '.'
